brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to test the safety and tolerability of BG-T0050 and to identify the recommended dose and dosing schedule (including dose levels and timing) that can be taken without having serious side effects in adults with DLBCL and other aggressive B-cell malignancies
primary_outcomes: Part 1a Dose Escalation: Number of Participants Experiencing Dose-limiting Toxicities (DLTs)
Part 1a and Part 1b: Number of Participants with Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs), Treatment-related Adverse Events (TRAEs), and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
title: A Study Investigating the Safety and How the Trispecific T-Cell Engaging Antibody BG-T0050 Works in Adults With Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and Other Aggressive B-Cell Malignancies

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy and safety of eloralintide and tirzepatide coformulation (EloraTZP) compared with tirzepatide, eloralintide and placebo for body weight reduction in participants with obesity.

Participation in the study will last about 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Percent Change from Baseline in Body Weight
title: A Study of EloraTZP in Adult Participants With Obesity Without Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) can identify previously unrecognized diabetes and clinically significant hyperglycemia in adults with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) receiving hemodialysis who have no known history of diabetes.

Participants will wear a Libre 3 Plus CGM sensor for up to 15 days and undergo standard diabetes assessments, including fasting plasma glucose and hemoglobin.

The primary objectives are to:

* Determine the prevalence of previously undiagnosed diabetes among dialysis patients using OGTT criteria.
* Compare CGM glucose patterns between participants with and without diabetes as determined by OGTT results.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of DM based on OGTT
title: Unmasking Diabetes in Dialysis With Continuous Glucose Monitoring

brief_summary: This study compares two standard ways of closing surgical incisions in children and adults with cerebral palsy who are having multilevel surgery on both legs (single-event multilevel surgery, or SEMLS). Each participant serves as their own control: all study incisions on one leg, chosen at random, are closed with knotless barbed sutures, and the matching incisions on the other leg are closed with conventional knotted sutures. All sutures used have an antibacterial (triclosan) coating. The main question is whether knotless barbed sutures shorten the time needed to close each incision. The study also compares wound complications, such as infection and wound opening, and scar appearance, rated from photographs by masked reviewers and by patients or caregivers, over the 6 months after surgery.
title: Knotless Versus Conventional Sutures for Wound Closure in Cerebral Palsy Multilevel Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this retrospective observational study is to analyze multimodal imaging (including CT, MRI, and other imaging modalities), clinical characteristics, and laboratory findings from patients with post-stroke thalamic pain who were treated at Aerospace Center Hospital between September 2023 and September 2026.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

What are the structural and functional brain imaging features (derived from CT, T1, DTI, and resting-state fMRI) that distinguish patients with different pain severity levels? What are the metabolic profiles (measured by MRS) in pain-related brain regions (thalamus, anterior cingulate cortex, insula) in these patients? Are there correlations between imaging biomarkers, clinical pain scores, and laboratory parameters? Researchers will review and analyze existing medical records, imaging data (including CT and MRI scans), and laboratory test results from routine clinical care. All data have already been collected as part of standard patient care. No additional interventions, tests, or patient visits are required for this study. This is a purely retrospective data analysis study.
primary_outcomes: Pain severity assessed by Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Multimodal Imaging Analysis in Post-Stroke Thalamic Pain: A Retrospective Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an intervention can improve mental health outcomes among pregnant and postpartum Latinas. The main questions it answers are:

Is a collaborative, community health worker and social worker intervention is feasible within a community health setting? Is a collaborative, community health worker and social worker intervention is acceptable among Latina individuals in Central Texas? Do participants experience an improvement in perinatal mental health outcomes during or after the collaborative intervention?

Participants will:

* Receive 3 community health worker and social worker sessions during pregnancy.
* Receive 3 community health worker and social worker sessions postpartum (up to 12 weeks).
* Complete a survey at three timepoints (baseline, 2 weeks postpartum and 12 weeks postpartum).
title: Improving Perinatal Mental Health Through a Collaborative, Community Health Worker and Social Worker Intervention

brief_summary:
Facial skin quality, including attributes such as skin smoothness, can be affected by intrinsic aging and environmental factors. The goal of this study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of NOA HYDRATION, an injectable gel designed for intradermal placement, in improving facial skin quality including attributes such as skin smoothness in Chinese adults.

NOA HYDRATION is an investigational device being developed for improvement of facial skin quality including attributes such as skin smoothness. Participants are placed into one of two groups - a treatment group or a control group (no-treatment control). There is a 1 in 3 chance that participants will be assigned to the control group. Approximately 150 adult participants seeking improvement in skin quality including attributes such as skin smoothness will be enrolled at approximately 7 sites in China.

Participants in the treatment group will receive intradermal injections of NOA HYDRATION to the facial area (excluding forehead, nose, lips, and periocular areas) on Day 1. An optional touch-up treatment may be given at Day 31. The treatment group will be followed for 12 months after the last treatment. Participants in the control group will receive no treatment for 2 months, then may receive optional treatment and will be followed for 9 months after treatment.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a clinic. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, questionnaires, photography, and checking for side effects.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Responder Status Based on Evaluating Investigator (EI)'s Live Assessment of Allergan Cheek Smoothness Scale (ACSS)
Percentage of Participants With Responder Status Based on Evaluating Investigator's Live Assessment Using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS)
Number of Participants With Adverse Events
title: Safety and Effectiveness of NOA HYDRATION Injectable Gel for the Improvement of Skin Quality Including Attributes Such as Skin Smoothness

brief_summary: This study will investigate the effects of local vibration and ankle joint mobilization on muscle tone, proprioception, and balance in individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. One group will receive local vibration applied to the gastrocnemius muscle, while the other group will receive ankle joint mobilization. Both interventions will be performed three times per week for six weeks. Muscle tone, ankle joint position sense, and balance will be assessed before and after the intervention. The study aims to determine whether these interventions can improve neuromuscular and balance-related functions in individuals with MS.
lead_sponsor: Gaziantep Islam Science and Technology University
title: Local Vibration and Ankle Mobilization in Multiple Sclerosis

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Ramipril works better than Amlodipine to reduce endothelial dysfunction in pediatric patients (aged 5-18 years) with end-stage kidney disease undergoing maintenance hemodialysis and diagnosed with hypertension. It will also learn about the safety, efficacy, and impact on quality of life of both drugs. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Ramipril lower asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) levels-a marker of endothelial dysfunction-more effectively than Amlodipine?
* Does Ramipril preserve Fetuin-A levels-a marker of vascular calcification-better than Amlodipine?
* How effectively do Ramipril and Amlodipine control blood pressure and improve disease-specific quality of life?
* What side effects or medical problems do participants experience while taking Ramipril versus Amlodipine?

Researchers will compare Ramipril to Amlodipine to see if Ramipril exerts superior protective effects on vascular health and endothelial function beyond blood pressure reduction.

Participants will:

* Stop taking previous antihypertensive medications (ACE inhibitors or calcium channel blockers) for a 2-week washout period prior to baseline testing
* Take either Ramipril or Amlodipine daily for 3 months
* Continue standard hemodialysis sessions (3 times per week, 3-4 hours per session)
* Provide pre-dialysis blood samples at baseline and after 3 months of treatment
* Complete the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL™ 3.0 ESRD) questionnaire at baseline and after 3-month
* Undergo regular blood pressure checks, clinical monitoring, and weekly phone check-ins to monitor safety and potential side effects
conditions: Endothelial Dysfunction in Pediatric Hemodialysis Patients
primary_outcomes: Serum asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) level as a marker of endothelial dysfunction
title: Ramipril vs. Amlodipine in Pediatric Hemodialysis Patients

brief_summary: A retrospective, multicenter chart abstraction to investigate the prevalence of chronic sialorrhea, and the real-world use of incobotulinumtoxinA injections in male and female participants aged 18 years and older with chronic sialorrhea. Patients who come to a neurologic clinic in the past 6 months from the start date will be screened by searching for the ICD-10 code and diagnosis of sialorrhea and cross-referencing with those patients also being prescribed incobotulinumtoxinA. Data will be retrieved from the electronic medical record.
primary_outcomes: Chart abstraction measured sialorrhea and its treatment in different neurological conditions
title: A Retrospective Chart Abstraction to Investigate the Prevalence of Chronic Sialorrhea, and the Real-world Use of incobotulinumtoxinA Injections in Male and Female Participants Aged 18 Years and Older With Chronic Sialorrhea

brief_summary: TACTIC-P is a single-center, prospective, single-arm study in 12 men with biopsy-proven prostate cancer and pelvic lymph-node uptake on preoperative PSMA PET, without bone or visceral metastases, who are scheduled for robot-assisted radical prostatectomy and extended pelvic lymph-node dissection. On the day of surgery, participants receive intravenous gallium-68 PSMA-11 followed by PET/CT and PSMA-radioguided surgery using a drop-in gamma probe. Resected prostate tumor, metastatic lymph-node tissue, and matched blood samples are used for high-dimensional immune profiling. The main goal is to determine whether functional pathogen-specific bystander tissue-resident T cells can be identified and quantitatively characterized in the primary tumor and/or metastatic lymph nodes. The study also evaluates immune features relevant to future personalized immunotherapy, the ability of PSMA-radioguided surgery to detect pathologically positive lymph nodes, and perioperative safety through 12 weeks after surgery.
interventions: PSMA-Radioguided Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy With Extended Pelvic Lymph-Node Dissection
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Evaluable Participants With Successfully Identified and Quantitatively Characterized Functional Pathogen-Specific Bystander Tissue-Resident T Cells
title: PSMA-Guided Surgery and Tissue-Resident T-Cell Profiling in Node-Positive Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
Prehypertension is an important risk factor for developing hypertension and cardiovascular disease. Promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors among young and middle-aged adults with prehypertension may help reduce the risk of progression to hypertension.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of an intervention based on the Behaviour Change Wheel (BCW) framework in improving health-promoting behaviors among young and middle-aged adults with prehypertension. The intervention will be designed to address factors influencing health behaviors and support participants in adopting healthier lifestyles.

The study will assess changes in health-promoting behaviors and related health outcomes before and after the intervention to determine whether the BCW-based intervention can improve lifestyle management in this population.
interventions: Behaviour Change Wheel-Based Health-Promoting Behavior Intervention
title: Behaviour Change Wheel Intervention to Promote Healthy Behaviors in Adults With Prehypertension

brief_summary: This retrospective comparative cohort study aims to compare the short-term clinical outcomes of ultrasound-guided sacroiliac joint (SIJ) injection, combined SIJ and multifidus injection, and multifidus injection alone in patients with sacroiliac joint dysfunction. Medical records of patients who underwent ultrasound-guided injection procedures were retrospectively reviewed and classified into three groups according to the documented injection target: SIJ injection alone, combined SIJ and multifidus injection, and multifidus injection alone. The primary outcome is the change in pain intensity during movement, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) from baseline to 30 minutes after injection. Pain outcomes at one week and changes in functional measures, including the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire and Oswestry Disability Index, are evaluated as secondary outcomes. The study aims to determine whether short-term pain and functional outcomes differ according to the injection target.
lead_sponsor: Fatih Sultan Mehmet Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity During Movement Assessed Using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Does Injection Target Matter in Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction?

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, longitudinal observational study aimed at characterizing the natural history of respiratory progression in adults with genetically confirmed Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The study will last 36 months and involve the retrospective and prospective collection of clinical, respiratory, motor, and genetic data from patients aged 18 years or older across 13 Italian centers.

Respiratory function will be assessed through spirometry, inspiratory pressure measurements, and sleep studies. In a subgroup of patients, diaphragm ultrasound will be used to evaluate diaphragmatic function. Blood samples will be analyzed to identify genetic modifiers and inflammatory biomarkers associated with disease progression.

The primary objective is to describe long-term respiratory progression in adults with DMD. Secondary objectives include validating new respiratory assessment methods, investigating the relationship between motor function, genetic factors, and respiratory decline, and identifying prognostic biomarkers.

The study aims to develop an open-source predictive algorithm to estimate individual risk of severe restrictive lung disease and respiratory failure requiring non-invasive ventilation, supporting personalized respiratory monitoring and clinical management.
primary_outcomes: Characterization of Respiratory Progression in Adults with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
title: Respiratory Progression in Adults With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.

brief_summary: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an orally administered gel formulation in up to 60 participants who meet the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Participants will receive either the investigational nutraceutical supplement or a matching placebo daily for 6 months. The primary objective is to quantitatively evaluate the effect of the nutraceutical supplement, compared with placebo, on hair growth in premenopausal and menopausal women using the phototrichogram method.
primary_outcomes: Efficacy of Nutraceutical Supplementation on Hair Growth After 6 Months
title: Evaluation of the Effect of a Nutraceutical Supplement on Hair Growth and Hair Quality in Premenopausal and Menopausal Women

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding ipilimumab N01 to standard pre-surgery treatment with radiation, chemotherapy, and sintilimab can improve outcomes for people with high-risk, locally advanced rectal cancer whose tumors are mismatch repair-proficient and microsatellite stable (pMMR/MSS). The study will also evaluate the safety of these treatments and whether some participants may be able to avoid major rectal surgery after a strong response.
title: Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Plus PD-1 Blockade ± CTLA-4 Blockade for High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (pMMR/MSS): A National Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether giving amino acids through an IV during and after heart surgery can protect the kidneys of children with congenital heart disease. Many children who have heart surgery using a heart-lung (bypass) machine develop a sudden decrease in kidney function, called acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI can lead to a longer hospital stay and other complications, and over time it may raise the risk of long-term kidney disease. Children with congenital heart disease often need more than one heart surgery, so their kidneys may face this risk several times. There is currently no treatment proven to prevent AKI in children after heart surgery. Amino acids are the building blocks of protein. Giving amino acids through an IV increases blood flow and oxygen delivery to the kidneys. In adults having heart surgery, this treatment lowered the chance of kidney injury, but it has not been tested in children. The amino acid solution used in this study, TrophAmine, is already used routinely in children's hospitals as part of IV nutrition.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does IV amino acid treatment reduce how severe and long-lasting kidney injury is in the first week after heart surgery?
* Does IV amino acid treatment reduce signs of damage to the kidney's cells, measured in urine samples?
* Researchers will compare children who receive the amino acid solution with children who receive a placebo (Lactated Ringer's, a standard IV fluid that does not contain amino acids).

Neither the families nor the medical team will know which solution a child receives. About 270 children younger than 18 years undergoing certain higher-risk heart surgeries will take part at three hospitals: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, and Nationwide Children's Hospital.

Participants will:

* Be assigned by chance (like flipping a coin) to receive either the amino acid solution or the placebo
* Receive the study solution through an IV for 72 hours, starting in the operating room
* Have routine blood tests during the first week after surgery to check kidney function
* Give urine samples before surgery, 6 to 12 hours after surgery, and on the first and second days after surgery
* Have their health followed for 90 days after surgery, including kidney function, time on a breathing machine, and time in the hospital.
primary_outcomes: Urine NGAL, KIM-1 and L-FABP levels
title: Pediatric Randomized Trial Of Amino Acid Therapy Evaluating the Incidence of New Onset AKI

brief_summary: The purpose of this research is to assess the impact of a telephone follow-up visit on rehospitalizations after ostomy surgery.
interventions: Wound, Ostomy, and Continence (WOC) Nurse Telephone Follow-up
title: Conducting Wound, Ostomy, and Continence (WOC) Nurse Telephone Follow-up for Post-discharge Ostomy Patients to Reduce Hospital Readmission

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn if MPC: VISTA, an online training program, helps teachers and health educators deliver Making Proud Choices!, a program that helps teens lower their risk of pregnancy and HIV/STIs. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does completing MPC: VISTA improve educators' knowledge, confidence, and teaching skills more than live virtual training or no training? Do students taught by these educators show improvements in their knowledge and attitudes about safer sex practices?
* Researchers will compare MPC: VISTA to live virtual instructor-led training and to a waitlist group (no training during the study period) to see if online training prepares educators as well as, or better than, live training.

Participants will:

* Be placed by chance into one of three groups: MPC: VISTA training, live virtual training, or a waitlist
* Complete surveys and a short teaching skills assessment before and after the training period
* Receive MPC: VISTA training for free after the study ends, if not already assigned to it
* (A smaller group of educators who go on to teach Making Proud Choices! to their own students) have those students complete surveys about their knowledge and attitudes before and after instruction.
primary_outcomes: Educator Knowledge of Making Proud Choices! Content and Related Sexual Health Facts
Student Knowledge, Attitudes, and Beliefs About Safer Sex Practices
Educator Teaching Skill Demonstrated via Response to Virtual Classroom Vignettes
title: Scaling Effective Behavioral Interventions With MPC Avatar-Based Virtual Training

brief_summary: This clinical study was designed to assess the safety and efficacy of long-term dosing of GW906
primary_outcomes: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), and TEAEs leading to treatment discontinuation
title: An Extension Trial of GW 906 in Participants With Essential Hypertension

brief_summary: This observational cross-sectional study aims to compare the levels of irisin, interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-10 (IL-10), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) in saliva and gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) among individuals with periodontal health, gingivitis, and periodontitis. Biomarker concentrations will be measured using human-specific ELISA kits. The study seeks to evaluate the diagnostic potential of these markers and to contribute to a better understanding of the inflammatory-metabolic axis in periodontal disease.
primary_outcomes: Irisin levels in saliva and GCF
IL-6 levels in saliva and GCF
title: Salivary and GCF Biomarkers in Periodontal Health, Gingivitis and Periodontitis

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to describe the clinical, biological, and radiographic characteristics at the time of cryptococcosis diagnosis, as well as the time interval between the initiation of BTK inhibitor therapy and the diagnosis of cryptococcosis.

And also, the clinical course of each patient at 12 months in order to evaluate the susceptibility to cryptococcosis correlated with BTK inhibitor therapy.
primary_outcomes: Microbiological and mycological data description of cryptococcosis
title: Cryptococcosis Associated With Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding ipilimumab N01 to standard pre-surgery treatment with radiation, chemotherapy, and sintilimab can improve outcomes for people with low- or intermediate-risk, locally advanced rectal cancer whose tumors are mismatch repair-proficient and microsatellite stable (pMMR/MSS). The study will also evaluate the safety of these treatments and whether some participants may be able to avoid major rectal surgery after a strong response.
title: Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Plus PD-1 Blockade ± CTLA-4 Blockade for Low/Intermediate-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (pMMR/MSS): A National Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This retrospective observational study aimed to compare three pain management techniques used after laparoscopic gallbladder removal (cholecystectomy): modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through the perichondrial approach (M-TAPA), external oblique intercostal plane (EOIP) block, and local anesthetic infiltration.

The study included 90 adult patients who underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy between January and April 2025. Patients were divided into three groups according to the pain management technique they received during routine clinical care, with 30 patients in each group.

The primary outcome was pain intensity measured 2 hours after surgery using a visual analog scale (VAS). Additional outcomes included pain scores at 15 minutes and 4, 8, 16, and 24 hours after surgery, the need for additional opioid pain medication, and opioid-related adverse events.

The study aimed to evaluate differences in postoperative pain control and the need for additional pain medication among these three techniques using previously collected medical records.
interventions: Modified Thoracoabdominal Nerve Block Through the Perichondrial Approach
title: Comparison of M-TAPA, EOIP, and Local Infiltration for Pain Relief After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a midwife-led digital prenatal yoga intervention via the MIDWIFEYOGA mobile application on birth and neonatal outcomes among 74 primiparous women. The intervention group practiced yoga twice weekly for 45 minutes using the application, alongside one weekly online session. Results showed that the intervention group experienced significantly lower rates of labor induction and analgesia use, shorter labor duration, reduced pain, and higher birth satisfaction. Additionally, neonatal birth weights, Apgar scores, and early breastfeeding assessment scores were significantly improved. A midwife-led digital prenatal yoga program provides an accessible, non-pharmacological approach to reducing obstetric interventions, enhancing birth satisfaction, and supporting positive early neonatal outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Duration of the Second Stage of Labor
Number of Vaginal Examinations During Labor
title: Effects of Online and App-Based Prenatal Yoga on Birth Outcomes

brief_summary: This randomised trial compares two treatments added to the same standard acne gel in people with moderate facial acne. All participants will use adapalene 0.1%/benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel at night. Half will also use clascoterone 1% cream (a non-antibiotic cream that blocks the effect of androgen hormones in the skin), and half will use clindamycin 1% lotion (a topical antibiotic), twice daily for 12 weeks. The main question is whether the reduction in inflamed acne spots (papules and pustules) after 12 weeks differs between the two groups. Secondary questions cover non-inflamed spots, overall clearance, skin irritation, side effects and patient satisfaction. A dermatologist who does not know which treatment each participant receives will count the acne spots at the start and at weeks 4, 8 and 12. Because antibiotic resistance in acne bacteria is increasing, the study will provide local evidence on whether a non-antibiotic option can be used as an alternative partner to standard acne treatment.
primary_outcomes: Percentage change in inflammatory lesion count
title: Clascoterone Versus Clindamycin Added to Adapalene/Benzoyl Peroxide for Moderate Facial Acne

brief_summary: This study evaluates 177Lu-AF03, a bispecific heterodimeric peptide targeting both FAP and integrin αvβ6, for safety, biodistribution, radiation dosimetry, and preliminary diagnostic efficacy in patients with malignant solid tumors. Preclinical studies showed enhanced tumor uptake, prolonged retention, and low uptake in non-target organs. Eight patients with confirmed malignant solid tumors will receive a single intravenous injection of 177Lu-AF03, followed by SPECT/CT imaging at multiple time points. Safety will be monitored until Day 7 post-injection.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and Severity of Adverse Events and Serious Adverse Events
title: Safety and Diagnostic Efficacy of 177Lu-AF03 in Patients With Solid Tumors

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to compare two ways of reducing pain during extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL), a non-invasive treatment that breaks up kidney and urinary stones with shock waves. Many patients find ESWL painful. In this study, adult patients (18-60 years, ASA I-II) scheduled for ESWL are randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) an ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB), an injection of local anesthetic near the spine on the side of the treated kidney; (2) an intramuscular injection of the anti-inflammatory painkiller diclofenac sodium before the procedure; or (3) no pain medication before the procedure (control). The main question is whether ESPB lowers pain scores during ESWL more than intramuscular diclofenac. Secondary questions include heart rate and blood pressure stability, the need for painkillers after the procedure, and patient satisfaction.
lead_sponsor: Sanliurfa Mehmet Akif Inan Education and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Mean intraoperative pain score (Visual Analog Scale)
Intraoperative pain scores at each time point (Visual Analog Scale)
title: COMPARİSON OF THE EFFECTS OF ULTRASOUND-GUİDED ERECTOR SPİNAE PLANE BLOCK AND INTRAMUSCULAR NONSTEROİDAL ANTİ-INFLAMMATORY DRUG ADMİNİSTRATİON ON INTRAOPERATİVE ANALGESİA AND PATİENT SATİSFACTİON DURİNG EXTRACORPOREAL SHOCK WAVE LİTHOTRİPSY

brief_summary:
This study is a multicenter, prospective, observational cohort study to evaluate the predictive performance of pre-treatment DCE-MRI-based artificial intelligence (AI) models for neoadjuvant chemotherapy benefit in locally advanced triple-negative breast cancer. The study plans to enroll eligible locally advanced triple-negative breast cancer patients receiving routine standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy and stratify participants into high-benefit and low-benefit subgroups via the established AI model based on baseline breast DCE-MRI images.

All enrolled patients will undergo systematic collection of baseline clinical-pathological data, pre-treatment DCE-MRI scans, neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimens, pathological complete response (pCR) status, objective response rate (ORR), and long-term survival endpoints including disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS). The primary objective compares the pCR rate between AI-defined high-benefit patients and published historical control data; secondary analyses compare ORR, pCR proportion, DFS and OS between AI-stratified high-benefit and low-benefit subgroups to comprehensively verify the clinical value of this imaging AI model for individualized neoadjuvant chemotherapy selection.
title: Pre-Treatment Breast DCE-MRI AI Model to Predict Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Benefit in Locally Advanced Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized, sham-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial will investigate the effects of bilateral transcutaneous cervical vagus nerve stimulation (tcVNS) on menstrual pain and related clinical outcomes in women with primary dysmenorrhea. Seventy women aged 18-30 years will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either active tcVNS or sham stimulation. The intervention will be administered once daily for 8 minutes during the first three days of menstruation. Outcomes will include menstrual pain intensity, multidimensional pain characteristics, dysmenorrhea-related functional and emotional symptoms, anxiety and depression, menstrual symptoms, analgesic use, and heart rate variability. Participants will be followed for five days during one menstrual cycle.
interventions: Sham Transcutaneous Cervical Vagus Nerve Stimulation
primary_outcomes: Change in Menstrual Pain Intensity Assessed by the Numerical Rating Scale
Change in Multidimensional Menstrual Pain Assessed by the Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire
title: Transcutaneous Cervical Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Primary Dysmenorrhea

brief_summary:
The vagus nerve is a nerve that controls many bodily functions, including stomach function. Investigators want to evaluate the effects of noninvasive stimulation of the auricular branch of the vagal nerve (ABVN) on vagal nerve function.

The purpose of the ABVN Phase 2 grant is to expand on previous work evaluating vagally mediated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). This will be accomplished through several independent, but related, studies. In this study, investigators will evaluate the effect of vagal stimulation through simple physical techniques (vagal maneuvers) in subjects with gastroparesis.

\[This study was originally described in NCT06491758, however a separate record has been created to more accurately reflect the independence of the individual studies supported by the ABVN 2 grant.\]
primary_outcomes: Amplitude of vagal nerve compound action
Respiratory Changes in heart rate during stimulation
Changes in amplitude of the surface electrogastrogram
title: ABVN Phase 2 - Vagal Maneuvers

brief_summary: Poor sleep quality and accelerated skin aging are common in postmenopausal women and may be linked, in part, through impaired vascular function. Avocados contain monounsaturated fats, carotenoids, vitamin E, magnesium, fiber, and other bioactive compounds that may support vascular health and, in turn, improve sleep and skin health. This randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether consuming one medium Hass avocado daily for 8 weeks improves sleep quality and skin health compared with a calorie- and fatty-acid-matched safflower oil control in postmenopausal women with poor sleep quality and overweight or obesity. The study will enroll 74 postmenopausal women aged 50-65 years who have poor habitual sleep quality. Participants will be randomly assigned to consume either one medium Hass avocado per day or 27 g of safflower oil per day for 8 weeks. Sleep will be assessed using wrist actigraphy, at-home electroencephalography, sleep diaries, and validated sleep questionnaires. Skin hydration, elasticity, barrier function, collagen, pigmentation, and wrinkles will also be assessed. Vascular function will be measured using flow-mediated dilation and blood biomarkers. The investigators expect that daily avocado consumption will improve sleep quality, skin health, and vascular function compared with the control condition and will explore whether improvements in vascular function contribute to improvements in sleep and skin health.
primary_outcomes: Change in Actigraphy-Derived Sleep Fragmentation Index
title: Effects of Daily Avocado Consumption on Sleep and Skin Health in Postmenopausal Females

brief_summary:
This study is evaluating whether afimetoran, an investigational oral medicine that blocks toll-like receptors 7 and 8 (TLR7/TLR8), can improve skin disease in adults with active cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE), with or without systemic lupus, whose disease has not responded to or who cannot tolerate antimalarial therapy. Participants are assigned by chance to receive afimetoran or a matching placebo capsule once daily for 24 weeks, in addition to their existing standard lupus care. Neither participants nor study staff know which treatment is given.

The study is run in two stages under a single protocol. Stage 1 compares two doses of afimetoran with placebo to select the dose. Stage 2 compares the selected afimetoran dose with placebo to confirm efficacy and safety. After the 24-week placebo-controlled period, all participants receive afimetoran for a further 28 weeks, for a total of 52 weeks of treatment. The main measures of benefit are the change in the CLASI-A skin activity score and the proportion of participants achieving a 70% improvement in that score at Week 24.
primary_outcomes: Percent change from baseline in CLASI-A total score
Proportion of participants achieving a CLASI-70 response (≥70% decrease from baseline in CLASI-A total score)
title: Phase 2/3 Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of Afimetoran in Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to examine whether ideomotor apraxia is associated with motor function, balance, walking performance, and independence in daily activities in adults with hemiplegia after stroke. Ideomotor apraxia is a condition in which a person has difficulty planning and correctly performing learned movements, despite understanding the instructions. It is common after stroke, particularly when the left side of the brain is affected.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Do participants with ideomotor apraxia have lower independence in daily activities, as measured by the motor subscale of the Functional Independence Measure (Motor FIM), than participants without apraxia?
* Is the severity of ideomotor apraxia associated with upper limb motor function, balance, and walking performance?

Participants will attend one assessment session during routine follow-up at the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Clinic. They will undergo standardized clinical assessments of apraxia, upper limb motor function, balance, walking performance, and independence in daily activities. No treatment, medication, blood sampling, or imaging will be performed as part of this study.
primary_outcomes: Motor Functional Independence Measure (Motor FIM) Score
title: Post-Stroke Apraxia, Motor Function, Balance, and Gait

brief_summary: The primary objective is to evaluate the main pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters, efficacy, and safety of goflikicept (GFC) in children and adolescents with colchicine-resistant or colchicine-intolerant familial Mediterranean fever (FMF).
primary_outcomes: Area under serum concentration-time curve for goflikicept (AUC(0-W16))
title: Goflikicept for Resolution and Prevention of Attacks in Pediatric and Adolescent Patients With Colchicine-Resistant or Colchicine-Intolerant Familial Mediterranean Fever

brief_summary:
This project will evaluate how well the immersive virtual reality psychological program works in residential care homes and how it can be used in everyday practice. We will test its effects on mood, well-being, social connection, and related outcomes, while also examining what helps or hinders delivery in real-world settings, including any adaptations needed to make routine use feasible.

It is needed to close the gap between success shown in controlled research and the realities of daily care, where staffing, management support, and diverse resident needs can affect results. By studying effectiveness and implementation together, we can learn whether the program works across different homes and how to sustain it over time.

Residents may benefit through improved mood, well-being, and feelings of social support. Care homes may gain an engaging, adaptable activity that fits limited mobility and sensory needs, and the broader community and policymakers may receive practical guidance to implement, scale, and maintain an evidence-based mental health program for older adults in residential care.
conditions: Older Adults Institutionalized in Residential Homes
title: A Virtual Reality Program for Nursing Home Residents With Physical Disabilities

brief_summary: This clinical trial evaluates the effectiveness of pre-procedural mouthwashes in reducing bacterial contamination in dental aerosols generated during ultrasonic scaling. Participants undergo a single-day clinical visit where they receive a randomized pre-procedural rinse (or control) followed by full-mouth ultrasonic prophylaxis. Viable bacteria in aerosols collected on agar plates surrounding the dental unit are measured to determine whether rinsing with an alcohol-free mouthwash containing 0.09% Cetylpyridinium Chloride (CPC) and 0.28% Zinc Lactate significantly lowers bacterial contamination compared to water, no rinse, or a 0.2% Chlorhexidine positive control.
primary_outcomes: Total Viable Bacterial Colony-Forming Units (CFUs) in Dental Aerosols
title: Effectiveness of Pre-Procedural CPC and Zinc Mouthwash in Reducing Dental Aerosols

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (DTMS) using the H1-coil can safely and effectively reduce suicidal ideation in adults diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The main questions it aims to answer are: (1) Does DTMS reduce suicidal ideation in adults with PTSD? (2) Does DTMS improve PTSD symptoms?. DTMS is administered together with a brief exposure procedure intended to activate trauma-related neural circuits before stimulation.
title: Deep TMS for PTSD With Suicidal Ideation

brief_summary:
This study tests whether a medicine called ixazomib is safe for people living with HIV, and whether it can wake up HIV that is hiding in the body so the immune system and treatment can reach it.

HIV can stay hidden inside cells even when antiretroviral therapy (ART) keeps the virus under control. These hidden cells are called the HIV reservoir, and they are the reason HIV is not cured by ART alone. Laboratory research suggests ixazomib may reactivate hidden HIV and also help kill the cells that carry it. Ixazomib is already approved to treat a cancer called multiple myeloma and has been given to a smaller group of people with HIV in an earlier study.

About 45 adults with HIV that is well controlled on ART will take part. Participants are assigned by chance to take either ixazomib or a placebo - a capsule with no active medicine - one capsule by mouth once a week for a total of 25 doses. Two out of every three participants receive ixazomib and one out of three receives placebo. Neither participants nor the study staff know which one a participant is taking.

Everyone continues their own HIV treatment throughout the study.

Participation lasts about 7 months: 24 weeks of weekly capsules and 4 more weeks of follow-up after the last dose. Participants come to the clinic for about 14 visits, and take their capsule 24 to 36 hours before each visit so blood samples can show the effect of the dose.

The main purposes of the study are to evaluate whether ixazomib is safe and tolerable, and to measure whether it increases the very small amounts of HIV in the blood compared with placebo. The study also measures the size of the HIV reservoir and how the immune system responds.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Ixazomib-Treated Participants With at Least One Grade 3 or Higher Adverse Event Related to Study Treatment.
Frequency of Ixazomib-Treated Participants Who Prematurely Discontinue Study Treatment for Reasons That Are Deemed Related to Study Treatment.
Post-Dose Plasma HIV-1 RNA Levels Measured by Multireplicate Single-Copy Assay (SCA)
title: A Clinical Study of Ixazomib to Reactivate HIV and Reduce HIV Reservoir Size

brief_summary: This multicenter, randomized, controlled, non-inferiority trial is designed to determine whether remimazolam is non-inferior to propofol for prolonged sedation in adult ICU patients requiring mechanical ventilation for ≥48 hours. A total of 274 patients will be enrolled across 21 geographically diverse hospitals in China and allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either remimazolam or propofol using centralized, computer-generated block randomization. The primary endpoint is time to successful extubation-defined as extubation without reintubation within 48 hours. Secondary endpoints include quantitative measures of sedation quality (e.g., RASS, time to target sedation), clinically outcomes (e.g., length of ICU stay, 28-day and 90-day all-cause mortality), and comprehensive safety evaluation (e.g., incidence and severity of hypotension, post-sedation delirium).
conditions: Critically Ill Intensive Care Unit Patients
title: Remimazolam vs Propofol for Long-Term Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated ICU Patients

brief_summary:
This study will test computer programs that help doctors read brain MRI scans. The programs use artificial intelligence (AI). The study includes people with epilepsy, a condition that causes repeated seizures.

Brain changes linked to epilepsy can be hard to see on an MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) scan. Different doctors may read the same scan in different ways. The researchers want to build AI tools that help doctors find these changes earlier. Earlier findings could lead to a faster diagnosis. They could also help doctors decide if a genetic test or a brain surgery evaluation is right for a patient.

The researchers also want to learn if AI can predict how well epilepsy surgery will work. If it can, surgeons could use the tool to plan an operation. The goal is to stop seizures while protecting parts of the brain that control speech and sight.

Who can take part? People with epilepsy who are treated at the Gaslini Institute or another study center Adults who give their own written consent Children whose parent or caregiver gives written consent People who do not agree to take part cannot be included.

What will happen? The researchers will collect brain MRI scans from about 2,000 people. The scans come from regular clinical care.

The researchers will replace each person's name on the scan with a code number. The coded scans go to a secure online portal. Study centers around the world share this portal.

One trained researcher will run the AI programs on the scans. The researchers will keep the scans for 2 years to build an image library. The researchers will compare the scans with health information. They want to find signs in the scans that show how epilepsy may change over time.

This study does not test a new medicine or treatment. It will last about 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Create a large database of brain MRI scans from patients with epilepsy of various etiologies, referred to multiple highly specialized centers worldwide
Develop artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that facilitate the detection of lesions on neuroimaging acquired during routine clinical practice
title: Artificial Intelligence for Brain MRI Analysis in Epilepsy

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 4, multicenter, open-label, single-arm study evaluating the safety and efficacy of elranatamab monotherapy in adult participants with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma in India. Eligible participants must have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including an immunomodulatory agent, a proteasome inhibitor, and an anti-CD38 antibody.

All enrolled participants will receive elranatamab; there is no comparator or control arm. Approximately 100 participants are planned to be enrolled across approximately 10 study sites in India.

Study assessments will include evaluation of disease response and monitoring of adverse events in accordance with the study protocol.
title: A Phase IV Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called Elranatamab in People With Multiple Myeloma That is Not Responding to Four or More Standard Treatments or Has Come Back After Several Standard Treatments

brief_summary: Children aged 6 to 17 years with IBS will be randomly assigned to either receive psyllium husk supplementation in addition to usual care or receive usual care alone. The study will compare gastrointestinal symptoms, quality of life, and gut microbiota between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Irritable Bowel Syndrome Symptom Severity Score (IBS-SSS) from Baseline to 12 Weeks
Change in Irritable Bowel Syndrome Quality of Life Score (IBS-QOL) from Baseline to 12 Weeks
title: Psyllium Husk in Pediatric IBS

brief_summary:
The aim of this clinical trial is to examine the feasibility, acceptability and safety of a 6-week intervention (MYOPAP) which includes oropharyngeal myofunctional therapy, physical activity guidance, and sleep hygiene education in university students aged 18 years and older with excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale score greater than 10). The study will also explore changes in daytime sleepiness following the intervention and the feasibility of the procedures needed to inform future controlled trail.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What proportion of participants complete the intervention?
* What proportion adhere to the home exercises (at least 3 days per week)?
* Do participants find the intervention acceptable, and what adverse events occur?

Participants will:

* Attend one in-person session for consent, assessment, and instructions
* Perform myofunctional exercises at home daily for 6 weeks
* Follow physical activity and sleep hygiene recommendations
* Report adherence through daily polls and weekly check-ins
* Complete the Epworth Sleepiness Scale and an acceptability questionnaire at week 6
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with Adverse Events
title: Feasibility and Acceptability of a 6-Week Myofunctional and Physical Activity Program for University Students With Excessive Daytime Sleepiness

brief_summary: This is a Phase 1, fixed-sequence, multiple-dose study in approximately 42 healthy adult participants. The study will be conducted in two parts. Part 1 will evaluate the effect of fosmanogepix, through exposure to its active moiety manogepix, on selected CYP enzymes and on the concentration-QT interval corrected for heart rate (QTc). Part 2 will evaluate the effect of manogepix on CYP2C8 and on selected drug transporters. The maximum study duration will be approximately 13.5 weeks for participants in Part 1 and approximately 12 weeks for participants in Part 2.
interventions: The medicine cocktail (caffeine, bupropion, flurbiprofen, omeprazole, dextromethorphan and midazolam)
primary_outcomes: Part 1: Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of the medicine cocktail when administered alone or in combination with manogepix at steady state
Part 1: Area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) of the medicine cocktail when administered alone or in combination with manogepix at steady state
Part 2: Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of probe substrate cocktail when administered alone or in combination with manogepix at steady state
Part 2: Area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) of probe substrate cocktail when administered alone or in combination with manogepix at steady state
title: A Multiple-dose Study Investigating the Drug-drug Interaction Potential and QTc Effects of Fosmanogepix in Healthy Adult Subjects

brief_summary: Insomnia is a prevalent global health problem, with approximately one in five Taiwanese adults chronically affected. Prolonged use of sedative-hypnotic medications carries risks of adverse effects, dependence, and unnecessary healthcare utilization. Although cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is internationally recommended as first-line treatment, workforce shortages and suboptimal patient adherence limit its reach. This project will develop an artificial intelligence-driven mobile application for insomnia that implements the CBT-I components of stimulus control and sleep restriction. Using retrieval-augmented generation and large language models, we will build a localized sleep knowledge base to deliver personalized, interactive sleep guidance. A pilot randomized controlled trial will assess the intervention's effectiveness in reducing insomnia severity and sedative-hypnotic use. We will subsequently pursue a large-scale clinical trial and iterative model optimization, aiming to deliver the first clinically validated AI-enabled prescription digital therapeutic for insomnia and to advance smart healthcare in sleep care.
interventions: AI-Assisted Sleep Education and Personalized Guidance
title: AI-Driven Digital Therapeutic for Insomnia: Development and Clinical Validation

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot study is to learn about the effects of semaglutide on brain reactivity to cannabis-related cues in adults with cannabis use disorder. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does semaglutide effect reactivity to cannabis-related cues?
2. Does semaglutide safely reduce the frequency of cannabis use?

Participants will complete five in-person study visits over 9 weeks, which will include interviews, questionnaires, and collection of biological samples for laboratory testing. fMRI scans will be completed at two visits. All participants will receive weekly injections of 0.25-0.5 mg semaglutide across 8 weeks.
title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Cannabis Use Disorder

brief_summary: The main aim of this study is to assess whether secukinumab treatment retention over 12 months in adult patients with moderate-to-severe plaque PsO receiving secukinumab in combination with a GLP-1 RA is non-inferior to that in patients receiving secukinumab monotherapy. The study will also evaluate adherence, long-term treatment retention, and healthcare resource utilization.
primary_outcomes: Time to Secukinumab Treatment Discontinuation During the First 12 Months of Follow-up
title: A Real-world Study of Treatment Retention and Adherence to Secukinumab in Patients With Plaque Psoriasis (PsO) With or Without Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist (GLP-1 RA) Co-therapy

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether perioperative mirogabalin can reduce postoperative pain and morphine consumption in female patients undergoing modified radical mastectomy for breast cancer.

Postoperative pain is common after breast cancer surgery and may increase the need for opioid medications such as morphine. Although mirogabalin has been used to treat certain types of nerve pain, evidence regarding its effectiveness for acute postoperative pain remains limited.

This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will include 50 female patients aged 18-65 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III who are scheduled for elective modified radical mastectomy at the National Cancer Institute, Cairo University.

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of two groups. The mirogabalin group will receive 15 mg orally approximately 2 hours before surgery and every 12 hours for 48 hours after surgery. The control group will receive matching placebo capsules on the same schedule. Both groups will receive standardized general anesthesia and multimodal postoperative analgesia, including paracetamol and ketorolac, when appropriate. Intravenous morphine will be administered as rescue analgesia according to a predefined protocol when the postoperative pain score reaches 4 or higher on a 0-10 visual analogue scale.

The primary outcome will be total intravenous morphine consumption during the first 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include postoperative pain scores at rest and during movement, time to first rescue analgesia, the number of patients requiring morphine, postoperative nausea and vomiting, sedation, dizziness, respiratory safety, hemodynamic changes, recovery from anesthesia, patient satisfaction, and quality of recovery.

The study will assess whether adding mirogabalin to standard multimodal analgesia improves postoperative pain control and reduces opioid requirements without unacceptable adverse effects. The findings may help clarify the potential role of mirogabalin in perioperative pain management for patients undergoing breast cancer surgery.
primary_outcomes: Total Postoperative Morphine Consumption During the First 24 Hours
title: Perioperative Mirogabalin for Pain Relief After Modified Radical Mastectomy

brief_summary: This is a multi-site, open-label, single arm study to evaluate the rate of smoking abstinence by the end of the study with healthy adult consumers of cigarettes when provided with an e-cigarette over a 13 week study period.
primary_outcomes: Impact of varying levels of access to tobacco flavor options
title: A Study to Determine the Effect of Access to Multiple Tobacco Flavor Options on Smoking Abstinence Among Primary Cigarette Smokers Using an Electronic Nicotine Delivery System

brief_summary: This retrospective, single-center observational study investigates the relationship between cognitive performance and return to work in patients with Long COVID. The study includes patients followed in the Long COVID day hospital at Hôpitaux Paris Est Val-de-Marne who underwent a neuropsychological assessment as part of routine care. Cognitive performance in executive functions, attention, memory, and processing speed is analyzed in relation to employment status at the time of assessment and six months later.

Verbal Short-Term Memory According to Return-to-Work Status at 6 Months

Mental Flexibility According to Return-to-Work Status at 6 Months
Inhibition According to Return-to-Work Status at 6 Months

brief_summary: This three-arm randomized controlled clinical trial evaluates the clinical efficacy and safety of needle acupuncture and laser acupuncture compared with placebo (sham) laser acupuncture as supportive care for patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, Stage IIIB-IV). The study aims to investigate improvements in lung cancer-specific quality of life, symptom burden, functional status, and sleep quality over a 6 to 8-week intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung Trial Outcome Index (FACT-L TOI) at 6-8 Weeks
title: Acupuncture and Laser Acupuncture for Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an eye cream containing 0.05% Vitamin K2 (35) (MK-7) works to reduce vascular-type dark eye circles in women aged 20-60 years. It will also learn about the mechanism of action of MK-7 through laboratory studies. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the MK-7 eye cream improve under-eye skin color (lightness (L\*) and individual typology angle (ITA°)) after 4 weeks of use?

Does the MK-7 eye cream reduce under-eye melanin content after 4 weeks of use?

Does the MK-7 eye cream perform better than a placebo eye cream in improving these parameters?

Researchers will compare the MK-7 eye cream applied to one eye area to a placebo eye cream (a look-alike substance that contains no MK-7) applied to the other eye area to see if the MK-7 eye cream works to reduce dark eye circles. This is a double-blind, split-face study, meaning each participant receives both products but neither the participants nor the assessors know which side received which product.

Participants will:

Apply the MK-7 eye cream to one eye area and the placebo eye cream to the other eye area twice daily for 4 weeks

Visit the clinic at baseline (T0), 2 weeks (T2w), and 4 weeks (T4w) for instrumental assessments, including VISIA imaging and Mexameter measurements

Be instructed not to apply any products to the designated test areas for 3-5 days before each assessment

Maintain their usual basic skincare routine (e.g., cleanser, toner) on areas outside the test sites

Provide informed consent before participating
lead_sponsor: Nanjing Ascend Biotech Technology Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Change in Individual Typology Angle (ITA°) of the under-eye area from baseline (T0) to Week 4 (T4w)
title: Vitamin K2 (35) (MK-7) Reduces Dark Eye Circles: a Mechanistic and Human Efficacy Study

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial will compare the effectiveness of liquid nitrogen cryotherapy and carbon dioxide (CO₂) laser therapy for treating palmoplantar warts, which are human papillomavirus-related skin growths occurring on the palms and soles.

The main question the study aims to answer is:

\- Does CO₂ laser therapy achieve complete wart clearance more frequently than liquid nitrogen cryotherapy after 12 weeks of treatment?

The study will include 88 adults aged 18-50 years with palmoplantar warts. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups:

* Group A: Liquid nitrogen cryotherapy at -196°C, using two freeze-thaw cycles once weekly for up to 8 weeks.
* Group B: CO₂ laser therapy administered weekly for up to 8 weeks.

Participants will be assessed at week 12 after treatment initiation by a consultant dermatologist who will not know which treatment they received. Treatment response will be classified as complete clearance (no remaining warts), partial response (fewer warts than at baseline), or no response (the same or an increased number of warts). The researchers will compare the proportion of participants achieving complete wart clearance between the two groups. Adverse effects, including blistering, ulceration, and infection, will also be recorded during treatment.
lead_sponsor: Bkahtawar Amin Medical and Dental College Multan
title: Liquid Nitrogen Cryotherapy Versus CO₂ Laser for Palmoplantar Warts

brief_summary:
This study is investigating whether botulinum toxin type A (Botox) can improve scar appearance after cleft lip repair surgery. Cleft lip repair is commonly performed during infancy, but visible scarring can occur as the incision heals. Botox may reduce muscle movement around the surgical site during healing, which could decrease tension on the wound and improve scar formation.

In this study, infants undergoing cleft lip repair will be randomly assigned to receive either Botox or a placebo injection at the time of surgery. Researchers will evaluate scar appearance during follow-up visits over the first year after surgery and will monitor participants for any treatment-related side effects.

The goal of this study is to determine whether Botox is a safe and effective method for improving scar quality following cleft lip repair.
primary_outcomes: Scar Quality Following Cleft Lip Repair
title: Cleft Lip Scarring After Botox

brief_summary:
Background and Objective:

Malnutrition is a common and serious health concern for older adults in the hospital. This study aims to understand how often malnutrition occurs in elderly inpatients and to look at the different factors that may be related to it. The goal is to help doctors better identify and care for older patients who are at risk of malnutrition.

Methods:

This study will look at older adults (aged 60 years and older) who are staying in the hospital. Participants will be assessed for their nutritional status using standard nutritional screening tools. The study will also collect general health information, such as age, body measurements, blood test results, and existing medical conditions. Researchers will then analyze this information to see which factors are most closely linked to the nutritional health of these patients.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Shanxi Medical University
primary_outcomes: Comparison of clinical and nutritional indicators
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of GLIM-Defined Malnutrition Among Hospitalized Older Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether taking oral tranexamic acid (TXA) for one week after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction improves recovery in adolescents and young adults aged 14 to 25 years. All participants receive standard intravenous TXA during surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does oral TXA lower knee pain at 2 weeks after surgery?
* Does oral TXA reduce the amount of opioid pain medicine used in the first 2 weeks?
* Does oral TXA improve knee range of motion at 2 weeks?

Researchers will compare oral TXA to a placebo (a look-alike capsule with no active drug) to see if oral TXA improves pain, opioid use, motion, strength, knee function, and return to sport.

Participants will:

* Take 3 capsules (oral TXA or placebo) once a day for the first 8 days after surgery (day of surgery through day 7)
* Keep a home diary for 2 weeks recording pain scores, opioid pills taken and any side effects
* Return for study visits at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, 9 months and 1 year for pain, motion, strength and function testing
* Complete a survey at 2 years
title: Extended Post-Operative Oral Tranexamic Acid Dosing After ACL Reconstruction

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled study is to determine whether nasopharyngeal tube oxygenation could increase the fraction of inspired oxygen compared with standard oxygen during a sedated procedure with spontaneous breathing. The main question it aims to answer is:

• Does nasopharyngeal tube oxygenation deliver higher fraction of inspired oxygen without increasing adverse events, compared with regular nasal cannula during sedation? Researchers will compare nasopharyngeal tube to regular nasal cannula to see if nasopharyngeal tube oxygenation deliver higher fraction of inspired oxygen.

Participants will:

• Receive regular nasal cannula or nasopharyngeal tube
conditions: Sedation in Non-intubated Diagnostic and Therapeutic Procedures
lead_sponsor: International Peace Maternity and Child Health Hospital
title: Efficacy and Safety of Nasopharyngeal Tube During Sedation

brief_summary: This study examined the comfort of late preterm infants (born at 34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks of gestation) placed in four positions after routine nursing care in a neonatal intensive care unit. After each of four night-time care episodes, every infant was placed sequentially in the supine, left lateral, right lateral and prone positions within a nest for 15 minutes each, and comfort was assessed with the Premature Infant Comfort Scale at the 1st, 5th and 15th minutes.
primary_outcomes: Premature Infant Comfort Scale (PICS) total score
title: Post-Care Positioning and Comfort in Late Preterm Infants

brief_summary: this study aims to investigate the effect of chronic high-risk alcohol consumption on the effective dose of oliceridine combined with propofol for painless gastroscopy, so as to provide a reference for rational clinical medication.
title: The Impact of Long-term High-risk Drinking on the Effective Dose of Osselidin

brief_summary: This study compared a test azilsartan medoxomil potassium tablet (80 mg) with the reference product, Edarbi® (80 mg), in healthy adults. The study included a fasting part and a part in which participants took the study medication after a meal. In each part, participants were randomly assigned to receive both products, one at a time, in a different order. There was a 5-day washout period between doses. Blood samples were collected before and at scheduled times up to 48 hours after each dose to measure azilsartan levels. The researchers assessed whether the two products produced similar drug levels in the blood and monitored safety. The study was designed to evaluate bioequivalence, not to treat hypertension.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University
primary_outcomes: Maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax) of azilsartan
Area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time 0 to the last quantifiable concentration (AUC0-t) of azilsartan
Area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time 0 extrapolated to infinity (AUC0-inf) of azilsartan
title: Bioequivalence of a Generic Azilsartan Medoxomil Tablet Compared With the Reference Product (Edarbi®) in Healthy Chinese Volunteers Under Fasting and Fed Conditions

brief_summary: Ureteroscopy is the most common surgical treatment for kidney stones. Although rare, sepsis after ureteroscopy can be a life-threatening complication, occuring in \<3% of patients. There are several risk factors for sepsis including history of positive urine culture, pre-existing ureteral stent, or patients with chronic catheters/tubes. We want to study if an antimicrobial solution with chlorhexidine can prevent infections if instilled into the kidney prior to starting ureteroscopy.
title: Novel Antimicrobial Solution to Prevent Infections

brief_summary:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is preceded by a presymptomatic phase featured by the presence of islet autoantibodies (aAbs) without (Stage 1) or with (Stage 2) dysglycemia. Clinical investigations targeting Stage 1 or Stage 2 disease have been using the time to clinical disease progression (Stage 3) as primary outcome, with a consequent need for relative high numerosity and prolonged follow-up.

Additional hurdles limit the feasibility of disease modifying therapy (DMT) trials for preclinical T1D, including the need for an established screening program able to identify those who might be eligible and the enrolment of relatively large cohorts followed until clinical onset. To overcome these major limitations, our group recently explored the use of mathematical metabolic modelling of beta cell function in the early disease stages of T1D and its ability to quantify the response to treatment. We gathered, for the current proposal, sites with an established screening program for family members of people with T1D. The evidence obtained in our previous experience led to the design of this trial aimed to test the effect of a calcium channel blocker - verapamil - on beta cell function, as quantified through mathematical modelling, in Stage 1 disease. While this drug was previously tested in children and adolescents in the early clinical phases of the disease (Stage 3), it has never been used in Stage 1 disease. Verapamil inhibits beta cell apoptosis in animal models and has been shown to increase C-peptide secretion in adults with recent onset T1D and in youths. We hypothesize that an earlier treatment with verapamil targeting people with Stage 1 disease, whose residual beta cell function is greater than those with Stage 3 disease, may result in prolonged preservation of beta cell functional mass - and, consequently, in delayed clinical progression.
interventions: Verapamil 120 Mg/24 Hours Oral Capsule, Extended Release
title: Preclinical Type 1 Diabetes: the VIP-1 Study

brief_summary:
Advanced Practice Nursing (APN) has demonstrated a positive impact on improving health outcomes in various international clinical settings. In Spain, however, its integration is still limited and variable, especially in specialized fields such as neurology and surgery. Existing evidence suggests that health education led by an APN can improve key indicators such as health literacy, self-efficacy, and patient satisfaction, although further research is needed in our context.

Hypothesis: Health education provided by an APN significantly improves health literacy, self-efficacy, quality of life, and the healthcare experience of patients seen in neurology and surgery nursing clinics.

Objective: To evaluate the impact of health education provided by an APN on health literacy, self-efficacy, quality of life, and the experience of patients seen in a neurology and surgery nursing clinic.

Methods: A quasi-experimental, pre- and post-intervention, single-group study. The study will begin after approval by the relevant Ethics Committee. The intervention will consist of providing comprehensive, individualized health education that includes information on the person's health history, recommended lifestyle habits and practices, available treatment options, identification of warning signs and symptoms, how to respond appropriately to them, available care pathways, and contact information for the unit. Patients seen by a Primary Care Team (PCT) in neurology and surgery nursing consultations will be included, with data collected at three points in care: before the intervention, after the intervention, and at 6 months. The primary variable is health literacy, and secondary variables are self-efficacy, quality of life, and patient experience. A pre-post comparability analysis will be performed on the variables studied.

Relevance: The results will provide applicable evidence to promote organizational models that integrate PCTs into specialized care, improving the quality of care and the patient experience, and guiding future lines of research and implementation policies. In turn, they intend to demonstrate the value provided by the EPAs on the outcome indicators and the experience of the people attended in the neurology and surgery nursing consultations.
lead_sponsor: Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron Research Institute
title: Effectiveness of an Advanced Practice Nurse-Led Health Education Program (APN-HEALTH)

brief_summary:
The vagus nerve is a nerve that controls many bodily functions, including stomach function. Investigators hope to be able to measure the activity of the vagus nerve when it is stimulated through simple physical techniques.

The overall purpose of the ABVN 1 grant is to evaluate the effects of noninvasive stimulation on vagal nerve function. This will be accomplished through several independent, but related, studies. In this study, investigators will evaluate the effect of vagal stimulation through simple physical techniques (vagal maneuvers) in healthy subjects.

\[This study was originally described in NCT04206540, however a separate record has been created to more accurately reflect the independence of the individual studies supported by the ABVN 1 grant.\]
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with Vagal Nerve Activation
Number of participants with an increase in surface electrogastrogram amplitude
Percent Change in Heart Rate Variability
title: ABVN Phase 1 - Vagal Maneuvers

brief_summary: This observational study aims to generate real-world evidence on the use of semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity receiving care through a digital weight loss service (DWLS) programme in Australia. The study will evaluate treatment patterns, adherence, quality of life, safety, and other health outcomes associated with semaglutide use in routine clinical practice. Information will be collected from data generated during standard clinical care, and no study-specific treatment or procedures will be required.
primary_outcomes: Absolute change in body weight from baseline
Percentage change in body weight from baseline
title: Semaglutide Health Outcomes and Patient Adherence in Australia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if home-based transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) works to treat fatigue and other symptoms in adults with Long COVID. It will also learn about the safety and home adherence of this intervention. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does active tDCS lower fatigue severity (FAS score) compared to sham treatment?

What are the effects of the treatment sequence on cognition, pain, anxiety, depression, and quality of life?

Researchers will compare a sequence of active tDCS followed by sham tDCS to a sequence of sham tDCS followed by active tDCS in a crossover design to see if the intervention works.

Participants will:

Receive a tapered schedule of home-based tDCS over 3 weeks per intervention period (totaling 42 sessions per intervention, separated by a 4-week washout period)

Complete symptom evaluations and cognitive/clinical tests at baseline, after Phase 1, and after Phase 2

Log their daily sessions to track home adherence and report any potential side effects
primary_outcomes: Change in fatigue severity measured by the Fatigue Assessment Scale (FAS)
title: Intensive Home-based Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Long COVID

brief_summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial will evaluate the effects of Ubiquinol and Ubiquinone on vascular endothelial function in generally healthy adults with borderline high LDL-cholesterol. Participants will receive Ubiquinol 200 mg/day, Ubiquinone 200 mg/day, or placebo for 8 weeks. The primary outcome is change in flow-mediated dilation (FMD), a measure of vascular endothelial function, assessed at baseline, Week 4, and Week 8. The study will also evaluate changes in plasma CoQ10 levels, nitric oxide, LDL oxidation susceptibility, oxidative stress markers, and treatment-emergent adverse events.
title: Effects of Ubiquinol and Ubiquinone on Vascular Function in Healthy Adults With Borderline High LDL-Cholesterol

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether an adapted group therapy works to treat anxiety and depression in adults with an autism diagnosis.

The therapy is a form of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). CBT is a talking therapy. It helps people work with their thoughts, feelings, and habits. This version is adapted for adults with an autism diagnosis. The room is quiet and calm. Each session follows the same plan. The group uses a workbook. The clinic already offers this therapy. No one has yet tested how well it works compared to usual care.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the group therapy help participants feel better overall after 12 weeks?
* Does it lower symptoms of anxiety and low mood more than usual care?
* Do participants still feel better 3 months after the therapy ends?

Researchers will compare the adapted group therapy with usual care. Usual care is the one-to-one follow-up that participants already get at the clinic. A computer places each participant in one of the two groups at random. This means chance decides, not the researchers and not the participant.

Adults can take part if they:

* Are 18 years or older
* Have an autism diagnosis
* Have anxiety or low mood
* Already get care at the clinic

Participants will:

* Keep their own therapist and their usual care for the whole study
* Start the group therapy now, or stay with usual care and get the same group offer later, about 6 to 7 months after the start
* Meet in a group of 6 to 10 people for 1 hour a week for 12 weeks, if they start the group therapy now
* Answer questionnaires on a phone or computer at the start, each week for 12 weeks, and again after 3 and 6 months
* Choose whether to wear a heart rate band during group sessions. This is optional. Participants can take it off at any time.

The study takes place at one outpatient clinic in Oslo, Norway.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Clinical Outcomes in Routine Evaluation - Outcome Measure (CORE-OM) Total Score at Week 12
title: Adapted Group Therapy Compared With Usual Care for Anxiety and Depression in Adults With an Autism Diagnosis

brief_summary: This is a single-center, observational, bidirectional cohort study evaluating the real-world effectiveness, safety, and quality of life associated with sevabertinib in Chinese adults with HER2-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer receiving sevabertinib as second-line or later-line therapy. The study will include both retrospectively identified patients and prospectively enrolled patients. The primary objective is to evaluate real-world progression-free survival. Additional assessments include tumor response, overall survival, safety, and patient-reported quality of life.
conditions: HER2-mutant Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
title: Real-World Outcomes of Sevabertinib in HER2-Mutant Advanced NSCLC: A Bidirectional Cohort Study

brief_summary: Graftless Periosteal Coverage Versus Xenogenic Bone Graft for Jumping Gap Management in Immediate Mandibular Molar Implants. Volumetric and density bone analysis as well as the secondary aesthetic and stability outcomes were assessed.
