interventions: Particulate Xenogenic Bone Graft with Collagen Membrane
title: Graftless Periosteal Coverage Versus Xenogenic Graft for Jumping Gap Management in Immediate Mandibular Molar Implants

brief_summary: Cerebral palsy (CP) remains prevalent among very (28-31 weeks) and extremely (\<28 weeks) preterm infants. Prematurity-related brain injuries (high-grade intraventricular haemorrhage, IVH or periventricular leukomalacia, PVL) develop usually during the first few days after birth and are a strong predictor of CP. Development of IVH or PVL have been linked to hemodynamic instability. Artificial intelligence (AI) provides an opportunity to detect patterns from continuous physiological monitoring data that are associated with prematurity-related brain injury. A dataset of extremely preterm infants will be collated from previous INFANT Research Centre study cohorts. A separate but aligned anonymous dataset will be obtained from the University of Graz. Continuous physiological monitoring data will be analyzed with AI algorithms to identify infants with the highest risk of brain injury.
title: Intelligent Physiological Monitoring to Predict Preterm Brain Injury

brief_summary: The subject of this study is to examine the effects of Ai Chi-an aquatic exercise method-on balance, mobility, muscle strength, quality of life, depression, fatigue, and cognitive functions in individuals diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), in comparison with land-based exercises. Developed to address the physical and cognitive symptoms associated with MS, this study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Ai Chi exercises-performed in water-as an alternative and/or complementary rehabilitation method alongside traditional land-based exercises. In this context, the research seeks to offer an innovative approach to enhancing the quality of life and functional capacity of individuals with MS.
title: Ai-Chi in Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis

brief_summary: Preoperative anxiety and loud equipment noises, such as dental drills, create significant stress and autonomic fluctuations in patients undergoing oral surgery. Brainwave entrainment using alpha-band (10 Hz) binaural beats is a non-invasive audio method designed to promote relaxation and activate the parasympathetic nervous system. The purpose of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of a 10 Hz alpha-band binaural beat track embedded in continuous rain sound on reducing perioperative anxiety, maintaining hemodynamic stability, and improving postoperative recovery in patients undergoing impacted third molar extraction. Fifty-four healthy adult participants (ASA I) scheduled for impacted third molar surgery will be randomly assigned into three groups:Binaural Beats Group: Listening to 10 Hz alpha binaural beats embedded in a rain sound via active noise-cancelling (ANC) headphones during surgery. Placebo Group: Listening to rain sound only via ANC headphones during surgery. Active Control Group: Wearing ANC headphones with no audio broadcast (noise cancellation feature only). Preoperative dental anxiety, hemodynamic parameters (blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation) at four distinct intraoperative stages, post-surgical stress levels, and 7-day postoperative pain/analgesic consumption will be measured and compared among the groups.
title: Effect of Alpha-Band Binaural Beats on Stress and Recovery in Third Molar Surgery

brief_summary:
Patients with chronic knee osteoarthritis who do not respond adequately to conservative treatment may benefit from genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation procedures. Both bipolar radiofrequency ablation (BPRFA) and cooled radiofrequency ablation (CRFA) are minimally invasive techniques used to reduce pain and improve knee function by targeting the genicular nerves. However, comparative data regarding their clinical outcomes remain limited.

This prospective observational comparative study aims to evaluate the analgesic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided BPRFA and CRFA in patients with chronic gonarthrosis. Patients with moderate-to-severe chronic knee pain who achieve significant pain relief following diagnostic genicular nerve block subsequently undergo either BPRFA or CRFA targeting the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior medial genicular nerves under ultrasound guidance.

Pain intensity, functional status, kinesiophobia, and quality of life are assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia (TSK), and the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12) at baseline and during follow-up evaluations at 3, 12, and 24 weeks after treatment. The study compares pain reduction, functional improvement, treatment responder rates, quality-of-life outcomes, and procedure-related adverse events between the two treatment modalities.
primary_outcomes: Responder Rate Defined as ≥50% Reduction in NRS Scores
title: Bipolar Versus Cooled Radiofrequency Ablation for Gonarthrosis

brief_summary:
This single-center cohort study integrates humoral immune response profiling (Phage ImmunoPrecipitation Sequencing, PhIP-seq) with circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) genomic and epigenomic features, exosome transcriptomics, and plasma metabolomics to discover and validate liquid-biopsy biomarkers of treatment response in breast cancer.

The study comprises four cohorts: (1) a retrospective pan-cancer cohort of approximately 1,000 patients with solid malignant tumor, using archived residual serum/plasma to construct a pan-cancer antigen repertoire and cfDNA mutational/methylation atlas, with priority given to patients who had available Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) data; (2) a prospective cohort of 800 women with non-metastatic (M0) breast cancer receiving standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC); (3) a prospective cohort of 100 women with metastatic (M1) breast cancer receiving standard systemic therapy; and (4) a control group of 100 individuals, including patients with benign breast disease (breast fibroadenoma) and healthy volunteers.

The primary objective is to identify biomarkers-autoantibody repertoires, cfDNA mutation clearance, methylation reprogramming, exosome transcripts, and metabolic signatures-associated with pathological complete response (pCR) to NAC, and to develop predictive models where feasible.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
title: Multimodal Liquid-Biopsy Omics Biomarkers of Treatment Response in Breast Cancer

brief_summary: 2.040 This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of creative drama workshops on the therapeutic communication skills and empathy levels of nursing students. Therapeutic communication is a fundamental skill-particularly in pediatric nursing-for establishing trusting relationships with children and their families and for enhancing the quality of care; however, existing literature indicates that nursing students often lack the desired level of proficiency in this area and that traditional teaching methods may be insufficient for developing these skills. Furthermore, it is reported that empathy development is frequently addressed primarily at a theoretical level, with limited opportunities for experiential learning. In this context, experiential learning approaches, such as creative drama, are considered potentially effective for improving therapeutic communication and empathy skills. The study employs a randomized controlled experimental design. The study population consists of third-year nursing students; based on a power analysis, a total of 52 students (26 in the experimental group and 26 in the control group) are planned to be included. Participants will be assigned to the experimental and control groups via randomization. The experimental group will participate in creative drama workshops once a week for four weeks, while the control group will receive no intervention. Data collection will utilize a Personal Information Form, the Therapeutic Communication Skills Scale for Nursing Students, and the Jefferson Scale of Empathy for Nursing Students. A pre-test/post-test design will be used, and the data will be analyzed using the IBM SPSS 31.0 software program. Statistical analyses will evaluate descriptive statistics, parametric and non-parametric tests, as well as group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects. This study is expected to provide evidence regarding experiential learning-based educational approaches aimed at developing therapeutic communication and empathy skills among nursing students and to contribute to the improvement of nursing education programs.
primary_outcomes: Therapeutic Communication Skills Scale for Nursing Students
Hemşirelik Öğrencileri İçin Jefferson Empati Ölçeği
title: The Effect of Creative Drama on the Therapeutic Communication Skills and Empathy Levels of Pediatric Nursing Students: A Randomized Controlled Study

brief_summary:
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal condition affecting women of reproductive age. In addition to physical symptoms such as irregular menstruation, hormonal changes, and changes in body weight, women with PCOS may experience increased stress, difficulties in maintaining healthy lifestyle behaviors, and reduced quality of life. Lifestyle behaviors, including healthy eating, physical activity, and stress management, may play an important role in improving overall well-being among women with PCOS.

This study examined the effect of a structured Lifestyle Modification Program on stress, healthy eating habits, health-promoting lifestyle behaviors, and PCOS-related quality of life among women diagnosed with PCOS. The program was based on the 5A's model: Assess, Advise, Agree, Assist, and Arrange, and was culturally adapted for women with PCOS.

A total of 30 women with PCOS participated in the study. Participants were recruited from the Gynecology Department of Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad, and were placed into an experimental group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The experimental group participated in a structured lifestyle modification program delivered through four sessions over two weeks. The program focused on healthy dietary practices, physical activity, stress management, and strategies for maintaining healthy lifestyle behaviors. The control group continued with routine clinical care.

Participants completed assessments before and after the intervention. Measures assessed perceived stress, healthy eating habits, health-promoting lifestyle behaviors, and PCOS-related quality of life.

The study was conducted to determine whether a structured lifestyle modification program could contribute to improvements in psychological well-being, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and quality of life among women with PCOS. The findings may help inform the integration of psychological and lifestyle-based interventions into the care of women with PCOS.
title: The Effect of Lifestyle Program Women With PCOS

brief_summary: In this study, Logistic regression analysis was used to construct a risk prediction model for ASO in diabetic patients. Guided by the HAPA model, a nursing intervention plan for preventing ASO in diabetic patients was constructed and verified, with the aim of reducing the occurrence of ASO in diabetic patients and providing a reference for improving the quality of life of diabetic patients in clinical practice
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University
primary_outcomes: Summary of Diabetes Self Care Activities, SDSCA
title: Construction and Empirical Research of a Risk Prediction Model for Preventing Lower Extremity Arteriosclerosis Obliterans in Diabetic Patients Based on the HAPA Model

brief_summary:
Clear aligners are thin, transparent plastic trays that straighten teeth gradually and are a popular, more discreet alternative to traditional braces. To help the traOptionalys grip and move the teeth, dentists usually bond small tooth-colored bumps, called "attachments," onto the front or back surfaces of the teeth. Although aligners work well for many types of tooth movement, they are much less reliable at turning (rotating) teeth that are twisted out of position, especially rounded teeth such as premolars and canines. Teeth often turn less than planned or tip and shift in unwanted directions. As a result, patients may need extra sets of aligners or a period of conventional braces, which takes away the main reason many people choose aligners.

This study will evaluate the clinical performance of the proposed occlusal attachment designed by the investigators, quantifying rotational correction along with any unintended movements of the target and adjacent teeth. The study is not designed as a device trial of the aligner system, but as an evaluation of a modified attachment configuration within routine clear aligner treatment.

The Primary Objective is to determine the degree of rotational correction that can be achieved in rotated canines and/or premolars using clear aligners with occlusal surface attachments. The Secondary Objective is to assess any unintended tooth movements, including buccolingual tipping, mesiodistal translation and vertical displacement.
title: A Novel Attachment Design for Tooth Rotation With Clear Aligner Therapy

brief_summary: The EVIDENCE-RM study is a nationwide, non-interventional retrospective study evaluating the clinical and medico-economic impact of remote monitoring (RM) in patients with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator (CRT-D). Using data from the French national health database (SNDS) between 2019 and 2023, the study compares clinical outcomes and healthcare costs between patients with and without RM, as well as between those monitored via the universal Implicity platform versus conventional manufacturer-specific solutions.
title: EValuation of prognostIc and Cost reDuction by tElemonitoring iN CIEDs Usual carE: an Updated Analysis Using 2019-2023 Data

brief_summary: This study aimed to compare the immediate effects of classical hands-on massage and percussion massage in individuals with neck pain. Participants were randomly assigned to receive one of the two massage techniques. The study evaluated changes in muscle mechanical properties, pressure pain sensitivity, and anxiety, as well as patient satisfaction and therapist fatigue. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the effects of different massage techniques in the management of neck pain.
title: Comparative Effects of Manuel and Percussion Massage in İndividuals With Neck Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized comparative clinical trial is to compare the analgesic effectiveness of ultrasound-guided Midpoint Transverse Process to Pleura (MTP) block versus Erector Spinae Plane (ESP) block in adult patients undergoing open renal surgery. The main question it aims to answer is:

Does MTP block provide postoperative analgesia comparable to ESP block, as assessed by postoperative opioid consumption and pain scores?

Researchers will compare MTP block with ESP block to evaluate postoperative opioid consumption, pain intensity, time to first rescue analgesia, and the incidence of adverse events.

Participants will receive general anesthesia followed by either ultrasound-guided MTP block or ESP block before surgery. Postoperative pain and opioid consumption will be assessed for 24 hours after surgery.
conditions: Postoperative Analgesia in Patients Undergoing Open Renal Surgery
primary_outcomes: The primary outcome is the total postoperative opioid consumption, expressed as I.V. Nalbuphine in mg in the first 24 hour postoperatively.
title: Ultrasound-Guided Midpoint Transverse Process to Pleura Block Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Patients Undergoing Open Renal Surgery :A Randomized Comparative Study.

brief_summary:
Parents of infants in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) face unique barriers to long-term breastfeeding and lactation. The physical and emotional demands of having a critically ill or premature newborn combined with the stress, sleep deprivation, and separation inherent to the NICU environment make it difficult for many mothers to sustain breastfeeding and lactation, even when they want to. At the same time, NICU mothers are at elevated risk for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and poor health-related quality of life, which can further undermine lactation success and overall maternal wellbeing.

PeliCaN Multi-Site Breastfeeding tests whether a trained postpartum doula, working directly in the NICU can improve breastfeeding and lactation outcomes and support maternal mental health through 6 months postpartum. Participants are enrolled during their infant's NICU hospitalization to receive either doula support or standard care, depending on the study site condition at the time of enrollment (control vs. intervention). Mothers in the intervention group will receive lactation education and support, and emotional and informational support from a NICU-informed doula for up to 6 months. Mothers in the usual care group receive standard NICU clinical care, including access to NICU lactation consultants, without study doula support.

All participants complete surveys at enrollment and at 6 months postpartum covering infant feeding practices, maternal mental health, and demographic characteristics. The study asks two primary questions: (1) Does NICU-informed postpartum doula support improve breastfeeding and lactation rates at 6 months? (2) Does doula support improve health-related quality of life and reduce post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms at 6 months? A subset of intervention participants, NICU staff, and lactation consultants will also participate in qualitative interviews and brief implementation surveys to assess how well the doula program works in practice across participating sites.
conditions: LACTATION IN MOTHERS WITH PREMATURE NEWBORNS
primary_outcomes: Breastfeeding and Lactation Rates at 6 Months Postpartum
title: Postpartum Care in the NICU Multi-Site Breastfeeding

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to characterize the clinical and radiological manifestations of delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) experimentally induced by an isokinetic eccentric contraction protocol targeting the shoulder rotator muscles in asymptomatic athletic subjects.
conditions: Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness Experimentally Induced
primary_outcomes: Composite Clinical and MRI Assessment of DOMS Evolution in Shoulder Rotator Muscles
title: Clinical and MRI Characteristics of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS) of the Shoulder Rotator Muscles Induced by Eccentric Exercise: An Exploratory Prospective Experimental Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether patient recovery after ulnar nerve transposition (UNT) requires a splint. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the effect that early versus delayed mobilization after UNT have on patient sleep quality differ?
* What are the medical complications, reoperations, and timeline of returning to work that result from this procedure like?

Participants will be placed in a stiff splint (that limits elbow movement) or no splint (that allows for earlier elbow movement) after this surgery. Participants will report their recovery through surveys measuring physical function, pain, and sleep. Researchers will compare the results between the two types of splinting.
title: Is Splinting After Ulnar Nerve Transposition Necessary?

brief_summary: The objective of this project is to determine the effectiveness of weighted blankets as an anxiety-reducing intervention for neurotypical adult patients with dental anxiety undergoing routine dental procedures at the University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine. This study will evaluate heart rate, subjective anxiety levels, and provider and participant perceptions of weighted blanket use.
primary_outcomes: Evaluate differences in psychological anxiety measure.
Evaluate differences in physiological anxiety measure
title: Weighted Blankets for Dental Anxiety

brief_summary:
The purpose of this research is to test an investigational device called the Defibrio AED (automated external defibrillator).

The researchers are conducting the study to determine if the Defibrio AED is safe to use and is able to restore normal heart rhythm after an episode of VF (ventricular fibrillation) or VT (ventricular tachycardia).

The study will enroll 25 subjects in the United States. Participants that experience VF, or polymorphic VT, or pulseless VT, during an electrophysiology study or procedure will be treated with the Defibrio AED to restore normal heart rhythm.

Electrocardiography data will be collected from the clinical records, along with medical history, laboratory results, and medications information.
title: Defibrio AED Study

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a dietary intervention can improve clinical and immunological outcomes in women with autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), including Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Graves' disease. The study will enroll premenopausal women aged 18 to 55 years.

The dietary intervention consists of the simultaneous exclusion of three groups of potentially pro-inflammatory dietary components:

* Gluten-containing cereals, including wheat, barley, and rye.
* Casein, the main protein found in milk and dairy products.
* High-glycemic-index carbohydrates, such as refined sugar, white bread, and white rice.

The primary objective is to determine whether the dietary intervention reduces serum levels of anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies, which are markers of thyroid autoimmunity.

Secondary objectives include evaluating whether the intervention improves:

* Fatigue and energy levels.
* Mood and emotional well-being.
* Gastrointestinal symptoms.
* Health-related quality of life.

Women following the dietary intervention will be compared with women who continue their habitual diet to assess the effectiveness of the intervention. Group allocation will be based on participants' choice at study enrollment.

Participants will:

* Follow either the dietary intervention or their usual diet for 12 months while continuing their prescribed medical treatment.
* Attend four study visits: at baseline and after 4, 8, and 12 months.
* Undergo anthropometric assessments (body weight and waist circumference), blood sampling, stool collection, and a telemedicine consultation with a thyroid specialist at each visit.
* Complete brief online questionnaires every month to assess dietary adherence, fatigue, mood, gastrointestinal symptoms, and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Change in serum anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibody levels
title: Impact of Restrictive Diets on Inflammation and Quality of Life in Autoimmune Thyroiditis

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy and safety of eloralintide and tirzepatide coformulation (EloraTZP) compared to tirzepatide for body weight reduction in participants with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes.

Participation in the study will last about 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Percent Change from Baseline in Body Weight
title: A Study of EloraTZP in Adult Participants With Obesity or Overweight and Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized study at Severance Hospital compares two subchondral drilling techniques during CARTISTEM implantation for symptomatic medial-compartment knee articular cartilage defects. Sixty participants will be allocated 1:1 to drilling with a 2-mm drill alone or sequential drilling with 4-mm and 2-mm drills. CARTISTEM preparation and implantation will be the same in both groups. High tibial osteotomy may be performed when needed to correct alignment.

The primary endpoint is the International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) Subjective Knee Evaluation score at 12 months after surgery. The study will assess non-inferiority of the 2-mm technique using a prespecified margin of 10.3 points. Secondary assessments include pain and knee function, MRI cartilage repair and subchondral bone findings, radiographic osteoarthritis and alignment, and second-look arthroscopy in participants undergoing plate removal after high tibial osteotomy.
conditions: Articular Cartilage Defects of the Knee
primary_outcomes: IKDC Subjective Knee Evaluation score at 12 months after surgery
title: Subchondral Drilling Diameter During CARTISTEM Implantation for Knee Cartilage Defects

brief_summary: This is a prospective, multicenter clinical study designed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of remote surgery using the single-port thoracoabdominal endoscopic surgical system in breast tumor surgery. Eligible patients diagnosed with breast tumors will receive robotic-assisted remote surgery. The primary endpoints include safety indicators and surgical effectiveness parameters. The study aims to provide clinical evidence for the application of this surgical system in breast cancer treatment.
primary_outcomes: Rate of conversion to open surgery
title: Safety and Effectiveness Study of Single-Port Surgical System in Breast Tumor Surgery

brief_summary:
Dysphagia is a commonly reported complaint among patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), particularly those who have undergone upper-airway (oropharyngeal) surgery. However, how surgical treatment for OSA affects swallowing function and oral function (oral frailty) remains unclear.

This prospective cohort study recruits adults with moderate-to-severe OSA from the sleep medicine clinic of Kaohsiung Armed Forces General Hospital, Taiwan. Participants choose their own treatment as part of routine care; the study does not assign or influence treatment. Participants who undergo OSA surgery form the surgery group, and those who receive non-surgical treatment (e.g., CPAP) or no treatment form the non-surgical group. Swallowing difficulty (EAT-10) and oral frailty (seven oral hypofunction indicators) are assessed before treatment and at 1, 3, and 6 months after treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in swallowing difficulty measured by the Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10)
Change in oral frailty (number of oral hypofunction indicators)
title: Effects of Surgery on Oral Frailty and Dysphagia in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary: Retrospective and prospective collection of brain and spinal MRI and MR angiography images from patients of all ages with a genetically confirmed diagnosis of Noonan syndrome.
primary_outcomes: Description of Neuroradiological Features of Noonan Syndrome
title: Neuroradiological Features of Noonan Syndrome and Genotype-Phenotype Correlations

brief_summary: In Egypt, oral diseases such as caries and periodontal disease are particularly burdensome, with implications for overall health and quality of life. The World Health Organization (WHO) has reported high prevalence rates for these conditions, underscoring the urgent need for targeted research and intervention . This study focuses on understanding the burden of these diseases in a dental school setting, which serves a diverse patient population, and explores their potential interrelationship.
interventions: Prevalence of caries and periodontal diseases
title: Prevalence of Caries and Periodontal Disease and Their Correlation in a Dental School in Egypt

brief_summary: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different techniques in the restoration of elbow flexion in post-traumatic brachial plexus patients as regards timing and degree of recovery.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of Elbow Flexion Muscle Strength
title: Elbow Flexion Reanimation in Patients With Traumatic Brachial Plexus Injury

brief_summary:
The primary goal of this study is to evaluate the myelo-protective effect and safety of Trilaciclib in participants with limited stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) who are receiving concurrent chemo-radiotherapy.

Researchers will compare Trilaciclib with placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if Trilaciclib works better in protecting the participant's marrow function while receiving concurrent chemo-radiotherapy.
primary_outcomes: The duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in cycle 1
title: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-blind, Multi-center Trial Comparing Efficacy and Safety of Trilaciclib Versus Placebo in Participants With Limited-stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two postoperative analgesia strategies in adult women undergoing breast surgery and to evaluate their effects on postoperative pain and quality of recovery after hospital discharge.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a patient education-based analgesia strategy improve postoperative pain control compared with standard analgesic management?
* Does the patient education-based strategy improve quality of recovery after hospital discharge?

Researchers will compare the patient education group with the standard care group to assess differences in postoperative pain intensity and quality of recovery.

Participants will:

* Receive either a patient education-based postoperative analgesia strategy or standard postoperative analgesic management.
* Complete questionnaires assessing pain, quality of recovery, and other aspects of health at specified time points.
* Be followed for 90 days after surgery.
title: Comparison of Two Postoperative Care Strategies After Breast Surgery

brief_summary:
Breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has different diagnostic characteristics from conventional mammography and may detect breast cancers that are difficult to identify using mammography. In a predefined study population in Thuringia, Germany, breast MRI was performed as the primary imaging examination for early detection of breast cancer instead of conventional mammography.

The primary purpose of this study is to assess the quality and performance of the MRI-based breast cancer early detection program. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study will evaluate the performance of breast MRI using MRI data collected for early breast cancer detection, subsequent diagnostic assessment and histopathological data, and longitudinal population-based cancer registry information.

The primary objective is to determine the sensitivity of breast MRI for detection of invasive breast cancer. Specificity, program sensitivity, interval breast cancer, predictive values, receiver operating characteristic measures, cancer detection and interval cancer rates, diagnostic assessment and biopsy rates, ductal carcinoma in situ, and tumor characteristics will be evaluated as secondary outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of Breast MRI for Invasive Breast Cancer
title: Breast MRI for Early Detection of Breast Cancer in Thuringia

brief_summary:
This randomized study will examine whether ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia (a nerve block) contributes to new or worsening peripheral nerve problems after blast-related limb trauma. Blast injuries themselves can damage nerves, making it difficult to determine whether later numbness, weakness, or neuropathic pain is caused by the injury, surgery, or the nerve block.

Adults with blast-related upper- or lower-limb trauma who need pain treatment will be randomly assigned to one of two standard pain-management strategies: regional anaesthesia plus multimodal analgesia, or multimodal systemic analgesia without a planned nerve block. All participants will receive appropriate rescue pain treatment if needed.

Neurological function will be documented before treatment and reassessed during hospital care and follow-up. The main outcome is a new or worsened peripheral nerve deficit 30 days after treatment. The study will also assess pain relief, opioid use, function, neuropathic pain, and safety events up to 6 months.
lead_sponsor: Ukrainian Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Therapy
primary_outcomes: New or Worsened Peripheral Nerve Deficit at 30 Days
title: Blast-related Regional Anaesthesia and Peripheral nerVe Injury Evaluation

brief_summary:
Objective The aim of this research is to evaluate how improving the technology use skills of older adults in nursing homes changes their perceptions of access to safe health information and the use of artificial intelligence.

Hypotheses H1: Improving the technology use skills of older adults in nursing homes changes their perceptions of access to safe health information and the use of artificial intelligence.
title: Technology Use, Safe Health Information, and Artificial Intelligence Among Older Adults

brief_summary:
Background: Globally, cesarean section (CS) rates are rapidly increasing. Although cesarean delivery is a life-saving surgical intervention, it can lead to adverse outcomes such as anxiety, decreased maternal satisfaction, and alterations in hemodynamic parameters. Hand massage, as a complementary nursing intervention, is considered an effective method for alleviating these issues by promoting physiological and psychological well-being.

Objective: The aim of this study is to examine the effects of reflexology hand massage and stroking hand massage on anxiety, satisfaction, and hemodynamic parameters in women during the early postoperative period following a cesarean section.

Methods: This study is designed as a single-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. The study population will consist of women who undergo cesarean delivery and are hospitalized in the Obstetrics and Gynecology Ward of Dokuz Eylul University Research and Application Hospital. The study sample will include women aged 20-35 years who undergo a term, elective cesarean delivery between April 2026 and January 2027, and are at their 4th postoperative hour. The experimental group will receive a 20-minute reflexology hand massage, while the control group will receive a 20-minute stroking hand massage (placebo). Due to the single-blind nature of the study, participants will only be informed that they will receive a "hand massage," without specifying the exact technique (reflexology or stroking). Satisfaction will be measured using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and anxiety will be measured using the State Anxiety Inventory (STAI) before the intervention and 30 minutes after the massage application. Data obtained from the study will be analyzed using the SPSS (IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 25) software. Descriptive statistics will be presented as mean, standard deviation, and median (minimum-maximum) for continuous variables, and as frequencies and percentages for categorical variables. The conformity of the data to normal distribution will be evaluated using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests. For the comparison of continuous variables between groups, the Independent Samples t-test will be used for normally distributed data, and the Mann-Whitney U test for non-normally distributed data. For within-group comparisons of time-dependent measurements, Repeated Measures ANOVA will be applied if the normality assumption is met, whereas the Friedman test will be used if it is not met. To compare time-dependent changes between groups, a two-way repeated measures ANOVA will be utilized for normally distributed data, and Generalized Linear Models or appropriate non-parametric methods will be employed for non-normally distributed data. Categorical variables will be compared using the Chi-square test or Fisher's Exact test when necessary. The statistical significance level will be set at p \< 0.05 for all analyses.
title: Reflexology Hand Massage After Cesarean Section

brief_summary:
The MunichFlu study is a prospective observational study investigating the incidence and etiology of respiratory viral infections following attendance at the Munich Oktoberfest, one of the world's largest mass gathering events.

Participants will be recruited during the Oktoberfest after providing informed consent. One to two weeks after the end of the festival, participants will receive an online follow-up questionnaire collecting information on demographic characteristics, medical history, Oktoberfest attendance, and the occurrence of respiratory symptoms or other infectious illnesses after their visit.

Participants reporting symptoms suggestive of an acute respiratory infection will be offered an optional nasal and/or throat swab for molecular detection and identification of the causative respiratory virus. In parallel, wastewater samples will be collected at the Oktoberfest venue and analyzed for circulating respiratory viruses to assess environmental viral surveillance.

To account for seasonal variations in respiratory virus circulation, parallel population-based surveys will be conducted in the German cities of Regensburg and Nuremberg during the same study period. The combined epidemiological, virological, and environmental surveillance data will provide a comprehensive assessment of respiratory viral infections associated with Oktoberfest attendance.
conditions: Respiratory Viral Infections Associated With Oktoberfest Attendance
primary_outcomes: Incidence of respiratory viral infections following Oktoberfest attendance
title: Respiratory Viral Infections Following Oktoberfest Attendance

brief_summary:
\### What is this study about?

This study compared whether adding the \*\*Spencer muscle energy technique (MET)\*\* versus conventional rehabilitation, following identical ultrasound-guided intra-articular corticosteroid-hyaluronate injection, improves shoulder outcomes for patients with painful-phase frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis).

\### Why does it matter?

Frozen shoulder causes shoulder pain and marked loss of range of motion, greatly impairing daily function and quality of life. The painful "freezing" phase is dominated by inflammation and pain-driven muscle guarding. Intra-articular injection can deliver short-term pain relief but cannot mechanically stretch contracted joint capsules; it therefore works best as a platform for subsequent rehabilitation.

Although the Spencer muscle energy technique is widely used clinically for frozen-shoulder rehabilitation, prior trials often combined it with variable injection protocols and lacked direct comparison against standard rehabilitation. It remained unclear whether any observed benefits came from the injection itself or from the manual therapy technique. This trial fixed the injection and pain neuroscience education for both groups, isolating the effect of the manual therapy approach.

\### What did the researchers do?

Patients with unilateral painful-phase primary frozen shoulder were randomised into two groups. All participants received one ultrasound-guided glenohumeral and subacromial bursa injection (corticosteroid, hyaluronate, ropivacaine and normal saline), plus standardised pain neuroscience education.

* \*\*Spencer group (n=33):\*\* 8-week programme of Spencer muscle energy technique
* \*\*Control group (n=31):\*\* 8-week conventional rehabilitation (joint mobilisation, manual therapy and stretching)
* Outcomes were assessed at \*\*baseline, 8-weeks (end-of-treatment), and 24-week follow-up\*\*
* Primary outcome: shoulder function measured by the Constant-Murley score
* Secondary measures: pain (NRS), kinesiophobia (TSK-17), mental quality-of-life (SF-36 MCS), active shoulder range of motion, and ultrasound thickness of the coracohumeral ligament and inferior glenohumeral capsule
* Outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to group allocation; safety and adverse events were monitored throughout the trial.
interventions: Ultrasound-guided injection of sodium hyaluronate, ropivacaine hydrochloride, and compound betamethasone
title: Effects of Injection Combined With Spencer Technique on Painful Frozen Shoulder

brief_summary:
Total hip arthroplasty can cause significant pain after surgery. Regional anesthesia techniques, such as the pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block and the suprainguinal fascia iliaca plane block, may help reduce postoperative pain and opioid requirements. However, these techniques may also affect muscle strength and early mobilization.

This randomized, controlled, prospective study compares the effects of PENG block, suprainguinal fascia iliaca plane block, and no regional block in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty. Postoperative pain, opioid consumption, quadriceps muscle strength, and hip flexion are evaluated to compare the analgesic effectiveness and motor effects of these approaches.
title: PENG, Suprainguinal Fascia Iliaca Block, and Control After Total Hip Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate how artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated into an organized breast cancer screening program for women aged 50-74 years undergoing mammography screening.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can an AI-based workflow that identifies selected mammograms for review by a third radiologist improve or maintain the cancer detection rate compared with the current AI-supported double-reading workflow?
* How would this AI-based workflow affect recall rates, biopsy referrals, false-positive results, interval cancers, radiologists' workload, and the number of cases requiring third-reader review?

Researchers will compare the currently used screening strategy, in which mammograms are independently read by two radiologists with AI support, with an alternative AI-based strategy reconstructed using a target trial emulation approach. In the alternative strategy, predefined AI score thresholds will be used to identify selected cases for an offline review by an independent third radiologist.

Participants will not be asked to undergo additional examinations or changes to their clinical care. Researchers will use routinely collected mammography screening data, AI scores, radiologists' readings, screening outcomes, and follow-up information. The alternative AI-based screening workflow will be evaluated retrospectively and will not affect participants' screening results or clinical management.
interventions: Discrete Choice Experiment on AI-Supported Breast Cancer Screening
lead_sponsor: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS
title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Breast Cancer Screening: The ANIHTA Study

brief_summary:
Asthma is a common long-term respiratory condition in children. In addition to affecting breathing, asthma may affect physical activity, exercise capacity, daily functioning, and quality of life. Respiratory muscles, particularly the muscles used for breathing in, play an important role in breathing and may also contribute to physical functioning.

The purpose of this randomized controlled study is to investigate whether adding inspiratory muscle training to a respiratory exercise program provides additional benefits for children with asthma. The study will evaluate the effects of the training using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, which provides a broad approach to understanding health by considering body functions, activities, participation, and related aspects of daily life.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will perform thoracic mobility and thoracic expansion exercises. In addition, one group will receive inspiratory muscle training for 8 weeks. Before and after the 8-week program, participants will undergo assessments of breathing muscle function, lung function, exercise capacity, autonomic function, physical activity, and quality of life.

The study aims to determine whether inspiratory muscle training can provide additional improvements in respiratory and physical functioning in children with asthma and to evaluate these effects from a broader perspective using the ICF framework.
title: Effects of Respiratory Muscle Strength Training in Children With Asthma

brief_summary: Umbilical hernias are common, and repair with mesh lowers the risk of the hernia coming back compared with stitches alone. Most evidence comes from lower-risk patients. Patients with obesity, diabetes, smoking, or COPD have more complications after hernia repair, and the best repair for them is unclear. Minimally invasive intraperitoneal onlay mesh (IPOM) places mesh inside the abdomen, which may cause pain and long-term mesh problems. Duramesh is a mesh suture that spreads tension across the repair and avoids placing flat mesh in the abdomen. This randomized trial will compare Duramesh repair with minimally invasive IPOM in 160 high-risk adults having elective umbilical hernia repair at Northwestern Medicine. The main question is whether pain on the day after surgery with Duramesh is no worse than with IPOM. The study will also compare complications, quality of life, return to normal activity, costs, and hernia recurrence up to 2 years after surgery.
title: Duramesh Versus Minimally Invasive IPOM for High-Risk Umbilical Hernia Repairs

brief_summary: The investigators are proposing to test an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) based bibliotherapy intervention as a self-help approach to hoarding disorder. Participants will be 60 adults meeting the clinical cutoff score for the Saving Inventory-Revised, a hoarding severity measure and will be randomly assigned to receive the intervention or to a waitlist control condition.
title: A Test of Acceptance-based Bibliotherapy for Hoarding Disorder

brief_summary:
This study was designed to assess the effect of dapagliflozin on body weight, blood sugar, liver enzymes, and blood fats in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), a condition involving excess fat accumulation in the liver. The study hypothesis was that changes in these measurements after 12 weeks would differ significantly between participants receiving dapagliflozin and those receiving placebo.

The study was designed as a randomized, single-blind trial at the Department of Medicine, Shalamar Hospital, Lahore. Planned enrolment was 146 adults aged 20-70 years with NAFLD confirmed by ultrasound and a body mass index of at least 29 kg/m². Participants were to be randomly assigned to two equal groups of 73. One group was to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg by mouth once daily for 12 weeks, while the other was to receive an identical-looking placebo tablet containing no active medicine. Participants were to remain unaware of their assigned treatment. Both groups were to receive the same advice regarding diet, weight reduction, physical activity, and management of metabolic risk factors.

The protocol specified measurements of body weight, body mass index, fasting blood sugar, HbA1c-a measure of average blood sugar-and liver enzymes before treatment and after 12 weeks. Blood fats, including cholesterol and triglycerides, and the ultrasound grade of liver fat were also included. Follow-up visits were scheduled every four weeks to assess medication use and record side effects. The planned analysis compared changes from baseline between the two treatment groups.
title: Effect of Dapagliflozin on Metabolic Parameters in Patients With Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease

brief_summary:
With effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), people living with HIV (PLWH) are living longer and are increasingly experiencing aging-related conditions such as frailty and sleep problems. However, most frailty research has focused on the general older population, and little is known about how sleep relates to physical and oral frailty in PLWH.

This case-control study compares sleep disturbance, physical frailty, and oral hypofunction between adults living with HIV receiving ART and sex-matched HIV-negative pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) users recruited from an infectious disease outpatient clinic at a medical center in southern Taiwan. The study also examines whether sleep disturbance (insomnia severity and daytime sleepiness) is associated with physical frailty and oral hypofunction, whether physical frailty represents an indirect pathway between sleep disturbance and oral hypofunction, and the roles of ART and serum Galectin-3 levels in predicting frailty among PLWH.
primary_outcomes: Number of impaired oral function domains
title: Sleep Quality and Frailty Among People Living With HIV

brief_summary:
This 12-month, single-site prospective observational study will prospectively monitor the recurrence of mood episodes while continuously collecting passive digital phenotypes in individuals with and without mood disorders. A total of 200 adults will be enrolled, including 100 patients with major depressive disorder or bipolar I/II disorder and 100 healthy control participants. Participants will complete five clinical assessments at 3-month intervals and will continuously wear a consumer wearable device and use the My Mental HERO smartphone application for passive sensing and daily mood recording. Structured clinical interviews will identify the occurrence, subtype, and day-level onset and offset of mood episodes during follow-up.

The study will examine longitudinal digital phenotypes associated with mood states and subsequent mood episode onset. It is designed to provide an independent validation dataset for digital phenotypes and prediction models developed in the preceding MentalHERO prospective observational cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07151846). Because the two cohorts follow closely aligned study protocols and assessment schedules, data from both cohorts may also be pooled for secondary analyses where appropriate.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) for Prediction of Clinician-Adjudicated Depressive Episode Onset
title: Digital Phenotypes for Predicting Depression_Validation

brief_summary:
Influenza vaccination is an important preventive measure for patients with heart failure (HF), but vaccination uptake remains low in China. Although previous studies have demonstrated the benefits of actively promoting influenza vaccination, scalable strategies to improve vaccination uptake among patients with HF after hospital discharge remain insufficiently evaluated.

The PANDA-BOOST trial is a prospective, pragmatic, open-label, two-stage sequential randomized clinical trial involving participants previously enrolled in the PANDA II trial. The study aims to evaluate whether sequential digital interventions using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted telephone calls and short message service (SMS) reminders improve influenza vaccination uptake compared with a single routine vaccination recommendation.

After an initial AI-assisted telephone call providing a standardized influenza vaccination recommendation, eligible unvaccinated participants will be randomized in a 1:2 ratio to a routine recommendation group or a sequential digital intervention group. Participants in the sequential intervention group will receive additional AI-assisted telephone calls approximately 14 and 28 days after the initial call. Those who remain unvaccinated and meet eligibility criteria at the third call will undergo a second randomization in a 1:1:1 ratio to no additional SMS, gain-framed SMS, or loss-framed SMS.

The primary outcome is influenza vaccination uptake within two months after the first-stage randomization.
title: Sequential Digital Intervention to Increase Influenza Vaccination in Patients With Heart Failure

brief_summary: This prospective interventional study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy during fiber-optic bronchoscopy in patients with respiratory failure. The study will assess oxygenation, ventilation, , procedural interruptions, adverse events, patient comfort, and clinical outcomes during and after bronchoscopy.
primary_outcomes: Change in PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio: Change in the arterial oxygen partial pressure to inspired oxygen fraction ratio (PaO₂/FiO₂)
Change in PaCO₂: Change in arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) from baseline before fiber-optic bronchoscopy to 2 hours after completion of the procedure.
title: Role of HFNC During FOB in Patients With Respiratory Failure

brief_summary:
Endometriosis is a chronic condition affecting approximately 10% of women. It is frequently associated with persistent or recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain. The mechanisms underlying pain in endometriosis are complex and may include direct stimulation from endometriotic lesions and local inflammation, nerve involvement, and alterations in central pain processing. In some individuals, sensitization of the nervous system may result in pain persisting despite limited ongoing tissue injury.

Surgery is an important treatment option for patients whose symptoms are insufficiently controlled by medical therapy or in whom surgery is indicated to improve fertility. The primary aim of surgery is to remove endometriosis lesions, thereby reducing symptoms and improving quality of life.

However, patients undergoing surgery for endometriosis often experience more severe postoperative pain and require greater opioid consumption than patients undergoing other gynecological procedures. They may also be at increased risk of developing persistent postoperative pain, defined as pain that continues beyond the expected healing period and persists for months after surgery.

Esketamine is a well-established medication used in anesthesia and pain management. Its pharmacological effects and safety profile are well characterized. It is commonly administered in patients with pre-existing pain conditions or chronic opioid use. Previous studies suggest that esketamine may reduce acute postoperative pain, decrease opioid requirements, and provide benefits in certain neuropathic and chronic pain conditions. However, its efficacy and safety have not been systematically evaluated in patients undergoing surgery for endometriosis.

The ENDPAIN trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of perioperative esketamine in patients undergoing surgery for endometriosis, with the goal of improving postoperative pain management and recovery.

Primary Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of perioperative esketamine in reducing postoperative pain in patients undergoing intra-abdominal surgery for endometriosis.

Secondary Objectives: To collect information on preoperative and postoperative pain in patients undergoing surgery for endometriosis in order to improve understanding of the mechanisms and risk factors associated with severe acute postoperative pain and persistent postoperative pain.

To collect information on the effects of other analgesic medications used as part of routine clinical care in participating centres and to explore potential interactions between these medications and esketamine.

Primary Endpoint: Postoperative pain measured using a Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) at 30 minutes, and at 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours after surgery.

Secondary Endpoints:

Hospital-free days within 30 days after surgery, defined as the number of days spent alive and outside an acute-care hospital during the first 30 postoperative days.

Opioid consumption during the first 48 postoperative hours. Quality of Recovery (QoR-15) score. Serious adverse events. Adverse reactions associated with esketamine, including hypertension, tachycardia, hallucinations or dissociative symptoms, sedation, nausea, and vomiting.

Persistent postoperative pain and other patient-reported outcomes assessed three months after surgery.

Trial Design: The ENDPAIN trial is a triple-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial with a follow-up duration of three months.

Participants will be enrolled on the day of surgery. Most study data will be collected during the first 48 postoperative hours. A follow-up assessment will be conducted three months after surgery and may take place either during a study visit or by telephone, according to participant preference and local site procedures.

Trial Population: Adult patients undergoing elective surgery for endometriosis will be eligible for inclusion.

Patients will be excluded if they:

Do not provide informed consent. Have a known hypersensitivity or allergy to esketamine. Have a current or previous history of ketamine or esketamine misuse. Have a medical condition in which esketamine is contraindicated, such as elevated intracranial or intraocular pressure.

Have severe systemic disease (ASA Physical Status \> III). Have severe psychiatric illness. Intervention: Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment groups. Participants allocated to the intervention group will receive esketamine 0.5 mg/kg following induction of anesthesia, followed by a continuous infusion of 0.15 mg/kg/hour until approximately 20 minutes before skin closure. Participants allocated to the control group will receive an equivalent volume of placebo consisting of sodium chloride solution (saline).
primary_outcomes: Time weighted longitudinal postoperative pain measurement over 48 hours.
title: Perioperative Esketamine Safety and Efficacy in Reducing Postoperative ENDometriosis PAIN (the ENDPAIN Trial): a Randomized Controlled Trial.

brief_summary:
Epilepsy is a neurological condition characterized by recurrent seizures. Children and adolescents with epilepsy may also experience emotional and psychological difficulties, including problems identifying and describing their emotions (alexithymia), difficulties regulating their emotions, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. These difficulties may affect social relationships and quality of life. However, these aspects have not been adequately investigated in children and adolescents with self-limited focal epilepsies (SeLFE) and idiopathic generalized epilepsies (IGE).

Purpose: The purpose of this study is to assess alexithymia, emotional dysregulation, anxiety, depressive symptoms, cognitive functioning, empathic abilities, and quality of life in children and adolescents with SeLFE or IGE and compare their results with those of healthy controls. The study aims to identify possible differences in emotional and psychological functioning between participants with epilepsy and healthy participants.

Study Design and Population: This is an Italian, multicenter, prospective observational case-control study involving approximately 100 participants aged 10 to 18 years. The study will include 50 children and adolescents diagnosed with SeLFE or IGE and 50 healthy controls. Participants will be recruited at IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini and Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria Santi Antonio e Biagio e Cesare Arrigo in Alessandria, Italy.

Study Procedures: After informed consent has been obtained from participants and their parents or legal guardians, as applicable, baseline sociodemographic and clinical information will be collected, including current medication use where relevant. Participants will undergo standardized psychological assessments and complete questionnaires evaluating cognitive functioning, alexithymia, empathic abilities, emotional and behavioral difficulties, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and health-related quality of life. Suicidal ideation and behavior will also be assessed in participants older than 12 years using a standardized assessment tool, as specified in the study protocol.

Expected Outcomes and Significance: By comparing children and adolescents with epilepsy with healthy controls, the study aims to improve understanding of the emotional and psychological characteristics associated with SeLFE and IGE. The findings may help identify emotional and psychological difficulties in young people with epilepsy and inform future research and clinical approaches to their assessment and care.

No experimental treatment is administered as part of this observational study.
primary_outcomes: assess alexithymia, emotional dysregulation, anxiety disorders, and depressive symptoms in children with self-limited focal epilepsies
title: Alexithymia and Emotional Dysregulation in a Cohort of Pediatric Patients With Epilepsy

brief_summary: Clinical validation of SMARTDIAGO, an artificial intelligence-based system for remote functional assessment of patients with musculoskeletal disorders and functional frailty. The study will compare remote assessments performed using SMARTDIAGO with standardized in-person clinical evaluations to determine diagnostic accuracy, agreement, and operational feasibility.
title: Clinical Validation of SMARTDIAGO for Remote Functional Assessment of Musculoskeletal Conditions

brief_summary:
Some people who have had weight-loss (bariatric) surgery do not lose enough weight, regain much of the weight they lost, see obesity-related diseases such as diabetes or high blood pressure return, or develop complications of the first operation. Many of them need a second, revisional operation.

This study reviews the medical records of adults who had revisional bariatric surgery between 2017 and 2025 at a single surgical centre. It describes which revisional operations were performed after each type of first operation and measures how much weight patients lost 6 months, 12 months and up to 3 years after the revision. It also records whether obesity-related diseases and quality of life improved after the revision, and looks at patient factors linked to better weight loss.
conditions: Insufficient Weight Loss After Bariatric Surgery
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Total Weight Loss (%TWL) After Revisional Bariatric Surgery
Percentage of Excess Weight Loss (%EWL) After Revisional Bariatric Surgery
title: Weight Loss and Comorbidity Outcomes After Revisional Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will create a national registry (a secure online database) of people with Noonan syndrome in Italy. Noonan syndrome is a genetic condition. It can affect growth, the heart, and other parts of the body. It is rare, so doctors have limited information about how it develops over time.

WHY IS THIS STUDY BEING DONE?

The researchers want to learn more about how Noonan syndrome affects people. They will look at:

Signs and symptoms of the condition How the specific gene change relates to a person's signs and symptoms How children and adults grow over time Health problems that may appear in the short or long term Growth hormone (GH) treatment: how well it works and how safe it is

The researchers will use this information to write advice for long-term care and follow-up. The registry may also make it easier to start future clinical trials for people with Noonan syndrome.

WHO CAN TAKE PART? People of any age and sex People whose Noonan syndrome has been confirmed by a genetic test People who agree to take part. Adults sign a consent form themselves. For children, and for people who cannot consent, a parent or legal representative signs.

People who do not sign the consent form cannot be included.

WHAT WILL HAPPEN? Doctors at the participating centers will enter health information into a secure online platform. The information includes personal details such as age and sex, health history, genetic test results, and treatments.

The doctors will first enter information for people they already follow. Later they will add new diagnoses and update each person's information as time goes on.

Doctors will also enter the results of the first heart check. They will add the results of follow-up heart checks, about every 2 years, when available.

The database is stored at the Gaslini Institute in Genoa, Italy. The study leaders are responsible for it.

About 250 people will join at first. About 60 more will join each year, for about 400 people over 5 years.

WHAT ELSE SHOULD I KNOW? Taking part is voluntary. This study does not test a new medicine or treatment. Doctors record the care you already receive.

People in the registry will get news about new diagnosis and care options. They will also be invited to join clinical trials.

The study will last 5 years. It may be extended.
primary_outcomes: Describe the clinical characteristics of a large population of individuals with Noonan syndrome and the possible genotype-phenotype correlation
Provide an online platform for healthcare professionals to report demographic and clinical information on patients with Noonan syndrome
title: Registro Nazionale Sindrome Noonan / National Registry of Noonan Syndrome

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of BRAND'S Essence of Chicken (BEC) on biological age. Biological age will be measured using epigenetic clocks \[DunedinPACE (primary), GrimAge, PhenoAge, etc\] and other relevant tools.

Participants will take BEC or a placebo every day for 1 year. Biological age measures will be taken at baseline and after 1 year.
title: Biological Age Study of Chicken Essence

brief_summary:
This retrospective real-world cohort study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of different radiotherapy target volume extents in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

Patients who previously received definitive or preoperative radiotherapy, with systemic treatment consisting of concurrent chemoradiotherapy with or without immunotherapy, will be identified from existing medical records. The study will not assign or modify any treatment.

Patients will be classified according to the radiotherapy target volume actually used in clinical practice, including the longitudinal gross tumor volume-to-clinical target volume (GTV-CTV) margin and the extent of regional lymph node irradiation. The study will compare locoregional recurrence-free survival, recurrence patterns, overall survival, progression-free or disease-free survival, treatment completion, treatment-related toxicity, lymphocyte reduction, and postoperative outcomes among different target volume strategies.

The aim is to provide real-world evidence to support individualized radiotherapy target volume selection in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
title: Radiotherapy Target Volume in Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in the Immunotherapy Era

brief_summary: Postpartum Anemia is common after childbirth and may contribute to tiredness and reduced wellbeing in mothers.This randomized controlled trial will compare two treatments for postpartum iron deficiency:intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and oral iron therapy .This study will assess whether intravenous ferric carboxymaltose provides greater improvement in maternal fatigue during the first 6 weeks after childbirth compared to oral iron.Secondary outcomes will be assessment of depressive symptoms and breastfeeding self efficacy .Eligible postpartum women with iron deficiency anemia will be randomly assigned to receive either intravenous ferric carboxymaltose or oral iron therapy and will be followed for six weeks.The study hypothesis is that intravenous ferric carboxymaltose will result in greater improvement in maternalfatigue and may also effect breastfeeding self efficacy .
primary_outcomes: change from baseline in Maternal fatigue total score on the Multidimensional fatigue inventory
title: Maternal Fatigue After Postpartum Anemia Treatment With Intravenous Ferric Carboxymaltose and Oral Iron Therapy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluates the efficacy of an 8-week dietary education intervention in adults with subthreshold depression. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a dietary education intervention or a befriending control condition. The dietary intervention consists of online dietary education and counseling designed to encourage a Mediterranean dietary pattern. The control group will receive online befriending sessions of similar frequency and duration. The study will evaluate changes in depressive symptoms and investigate changes in oral and gut microbiota, dietary measures, psychiatric symptoms, metabolic measures, and neurobiological markers.
primary_outcomes: Change in Depressive Symptoms Assessed by the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D)
title: Dietary Education Intervention for Subthreshold Depression (MIND-Trial)

brief_summary: The overall objective of this study is to determine whether ROTEM (rotational thromboelastometry) guided dosing of four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) results in superior perioperative bleeding control compared to clinician-directed. PCC administration in adult patients undergoing high-risk cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) who develop post-CPB coagulopathic bleeding.
title: Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC)

brief_summary:
Obesity is a multifactorial chronic disease whose prevalence is steadily increasing worldwide, with substantial clinical, functional, psychological, and economic consequences. Body mass index (BMI) and staging systems such as the Edmonton Obesity Staging System (EOSS) allow obesity severity and associated cardiometabolic risk to be assessed, but they do not fully capture the complexity of the condition.

Although its etiology is not yet fully understood, obesity results from the interaction of multiple factors. Individual susceptibility, including a hereditary component, interacts with psychobehavioral factors such as dysfunctional eating patterns and sedentary behavior, endocrine disorders in some cases, and broader sociocultural and environmental determinants, including socioeconomic status and lifestyle. This etiological complexity is reflected in the wide-ranging impact of obesity on health: in addition to increasing the risk of numerous clinical complications, obesity can substantially affect psychosocial well-being and quality of life.

Given this multifactorial nature, current evidence and clinical guidelines support interventions that move beyond unidimensional approaches and address multiple dimensions of the condition in an integrated manner. The present study aims to evaluate the efficacy of an integrated multidisciplinary approach to obesity management compared with usual clinical care. The study hypothesis is that the combination of personalized nutritional, physiotherapeutic, and psychotherapeutic interventions can promote greater and more sustained weight loss, as well as better psycho-physiological outcomes.
title: MORPH-A - Multidisciplinary Obesity Rehabilitation & Psychophysical Health and Awareness

brief_summary: This study will test two approaches to reduce HIV-related stigma and improve quality of life and viral suppression among women living with HIV in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Twenty health facilities will take part. One approach will help facility staff reduce stigma, while the other will use group sessions to help women manage internalized stigma. The study will include 680 women living with HIV who have missed clinic visits or attended the most recent clinic visit 14 or more days late and will follow them for 12 months. Researchers will assess quality of life and viral suppression as well as how well the approaches are delivered, what supports or limits their success, and their initial costs. A study advisory group-including women living with HIV, community partners, health care providers, and Ministry of Health representatives-will help refine the approaches, interpret the findings, and guide recommendations for wider use.
primary_outcomes: Change in quality of life among women living with HIV (participants), measured using the WHO Quality of Life-Brief (WHOQOL-BREF).
title: Testing a Multi-Level Approach to Reduce Stigma for Women Living With HIV

brief_summary:
The goal of the SPICE-CF feasibility trial is to learn whether it is feasible to recruit and retain people with cystic fibrosis (CF) who are unable to produce sputum spontaneously in a study comparing two different nebuliser devices for sputum induction. The study will also assess how acceptable and practical the sputum induction procedures are.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is it feasible to recruit and retain people with cystic fibrosis in a study comparing two nebuliser devices for sputum induction?
* Can sputum be successfully obtained using each nebuliser device?
* How acceptable are the two nebuliser devices to participants?
* How long does sputum induction take with each device?
* What microorganisms are identified in sputum collected using each device?
* Can a visual scoring system be used to distinguish sputum from saliva and describe sputum characteristics?

Researchers will compare a jet nebuliser with an E-flow Rapid nebuliser. Each participant will undergo sputum induction using both devices, with the order in which the devices are used determined at random.

Participants will:

* Attend two study visits, separated by at least 2 weeks
* Receive a bronchodilator before sputum induction
* Inhale hypertonic saline using either the jet nebuliser or E-flow Rapid nebuliser
* Perform their usual airway clearance technique with supervision from a physiotherapist
* Have their lung function, oxygen levels, heart rate, and chest sounds monitored
* Provide sputum produced during the procedure for assessment and routine microbiological testing

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether it is practical to introduce a consistent monitoring approach to the right side of the heart in patients supported with VV-ECMO.

VV-ECMO is a life support machine that takes over the work of the lungs to give them time to recover. It is used when lung injury is life-threatening.

Whilst receiving VV-ECMO support, in addition to the current standard of care, the following will be performed twice weekly:

* Heart scan (echocardiogram)
* Blood tests (hs-troponin and NT-proBNP)

The patient's involvement in the study lasts for as long as they are on the life support machine, plus one final heart scan 48 hours after it is removed.
title: Right Heart Injury Monitoring on ECMO

brief_summary:
Unlike traditional physical exercise, the impact of singing on cardiovascular health has not been extensively studied. Endothelial dysfunction predicts cardiovascular events, and physical exercise improves vascular endothelial function. In a rigorously conducted randomized, cross-over control study, our team is the first to demonstrate that 30 minutes of solo singing improves endothelial function acutely, regardless of singing expertise. Changes were more robust in subjects with baseline endothelial dysfunction (i.e., those with established coronary artery disease). The improvements occurred in microvascular, but not macrovascular, endothelial function. The observed change in microvascular function translates into a \~25% reduction in cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, which is comparable to traditional cardiac rehabilitation program participation.

Based on our prior research, the overall objective of the planned future RCT is to test our central hypothesis that habitual singing over several weeks, similar to habitual exercise, will lead to sustained and favorable vascular adaptation, thereby lowering CVD risk. The overall objective of this project, titled "GrOup singing or solo singing To improve Vascular health in Older adults wIth Coronary artery disEase (GOT VOICE): A Feasibility Study", is to refine and protocolize the singing interventions and test the feasibility of our future trial design.
title: GOT VOICE GROUP SINGING

brief_summary:
Melasma is a common, long-lasting pigmentation disorder of the face. Some patients improve well with treatment and others improve little, and there is no simple way to predict this at the first visit. Recent studies suggest that melasma with more visible blood-vessel involvement may respond less well to treatment.

This study will assess whether the amount of vascular involvement seen on dermoscopy before treatment is associated with melasma severity after 12 weeks of oral tranexamic acid.

Adults with facial melasma (Fitzpatrick skin types III-V) attending the Department of Dermatology, Allied Hospital-I, Faisalabad, will take oral tranexamic acid 250 mg twice daily for 12 weeks, with a standard sunscreen and a plain moisturiser. Melasma severity (mMASI) will be scored at baseline and at weeks 4, 8 and 12. A dermoscopic vascular score will be recorded at baseline and week 12.
primary_outcomes: Week-12 mMASI in relation to baseline dermoscopic vascular score
title: Baseline Dermoscopic Vascular Score and Response to Oral Tranexamic Acid in Facial Melasma

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether monitoring perioperative inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers can help identify postoperative complications early in adult patients undergoing colorectal or gastric cancer surgery.

The study is a randomized controlled trial conducted at Bucharest Emergency Clinical Hospital, Romania. Participants are assigned to either an intervention group receiving enhanced recovery care (ERAS) combined with perioperative biomarker monitoring or a control group receiving standard postoperative care.

The biomarkers of interest include procalcitonin, lactate, and blood glucose. The study will examine their relationship with postoperative complications, particularly infections and anastomotic leakage.

Participants will be followed for 30 days after surgery to assess postoperative complications, hospital length of stay, readmissions, and mortality.

The findings may help improve postoperative monitoring and support earlier recognition of complications in patients undergoing cancer surgery.
primary_outcomes: Predictive Performance of Perioperative Biomarkers for Postoperative Complications
title: Perioperative Biomarkers in Colorectal and Gastric Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, single-blinded, randomized controlled trial conducted at The First Hospital of Jilin University. A total of 134 adult patients aged 18-65 years with ASA Ⅰ-Ⅲ undergoing elective laryngoscopic surgery for vocal cord polyps will be enrolled. Subjects will be randomly assigned into two groups. The control group receives intranasal dexmedetomidine plus intravenous normal saline before anesthesia induction. The combination group receives the same dose of intranasal dexmedetomidine plus intravenous esketamine before induction. The primary objective is to compare the incidence of emergence agitation within 60 minutes after extubation. Secondary outcomes include hemodynamic changes, adverse events, recovery time, PACU stay, postoperative sore throat pain and quality of recovery at 24 hours. Standardized anesthesia induction and maintenance will be applied for all patients. The study aims to explore whether the combination of intranasal dexmedetomidine and esketamine improves recovery quality in patients undergoing suspension laryngoscopy.
lead_sponsor: The First Hospital of Jilin University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of emergence agitation within 60 minutes after surgery
title: Intranasal Dexmedetomidine Combined With Esketamine for Emergence Quality After Suspension Laryngoscopy
