brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot study is to determine the feasibility and to learn if a training program called E2NGAGE-Literacy (Empowering Elders in Navigating Generative AI for Greater E-health Literacy) can potentially help older adults in Singapore use generative AI (GenAI) chatbots safely and confidently to find and evaluate health information.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the conduct of E2NGAGE-Literacy program to improve older adults' AI literacy and digital health literacy feasible?
* Do older adults find the E2NGAGE-Literacy program acceptable?
* What are the potential changes in AI literacy, digital health literacy and actual use of AI-chatbot apps and web-based apps between older adults who receive E2NGAGE-Literacy program and those who do not receive the program?
* What do participants think about E2NGAGE-Literacy, and how can it be improved?

Researchers will compare two groups:

* E2NGAGE-Literacy group: Participants will join a 6-week program with face-to-face group lessons on using GenAI for health information, supported by online videos, quizzes and short homework tasks.
* Waitlist control group: Participants will continue with their usual activities at the senior centres and receive the same program after the study period.

Participants in the E2NGAGE-Literacy group will:

* Join weekly 1.5-hour face-to-face sessions for 6 weeks during the study period
* Watch short videos and complete online quizzes and practice tasks between sessions during the study period
* Be invited to a focus group discussion after the program to share their experiences
* Complete a questionnaire at the start of the study and again at 7 and 12 weeks later
* Be invited to share AI-chatbot transcripts for analysis

Participants in the waitlist group will:

* Complete a questionnaire at the start of the study and again at 7 and 12 weeks later
* Join weekly 1.5-hour face-to-face sessions for 6 weeks after the study period (after week 8)
* Watch short videos and complete online quizzes and practice tasks between sessions after the study period (after week 12)
* Be invited to share AI-chatbot transcripts for analysis
interventions: AI and digital health literacy program (E2NGAGE-Literacy)
title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Health Literacies Among Older Adults: A Mixed-method Pilot Intervention Study

brief_summary: This study will adopt a prospective, single-center, single-arm research design, enrolling 120 patients with paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation who are scheduled to undergo catheter ablation for the first time. Individualized pulsed electrical field pulmonary vein isolation will be performed under the guidance of pulmonary vein vestibular stromal mapping. By recording the distribution characteristics of abnormal stroma in the pulmonary vein vestibule, the guidance situation of the ablation strategy based on the mapping results, surgical and ablation parameters, immediate pulmonary vein isolation effect, perioperative complications, and the 12-month recurrence-free survival rate of atrial arrhythmias after surgery, the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of this ablation strategy will be evaluated, and the relationship between the characteristics of pulmonary vein vestibular stroma and postoperative recurrence will be explored. This will provide more clinical experience and data support for individualized ablation under the guidance of pulmonary vein vestibular stromal mapping.
interventions: Individualized Pulsed Field Ablation Guided by Pulmonary Vein Antral Substrate Mapping
title: Efficacy and Safety of Individualized Pulsed Field Ablation Guided by Pulmonary Vein Antral Substrate Mapping for Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective, Single-Center, Single-Arm Study

brief_summary:
This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, prospective, non-profit study.

Patients who provide informed consent to participate will be asked to provide a peripheral blood sample, a fresh tumor tissue sample (obtained by biopsy), and/or a bone marrow sample.

All patients with neuroblastoma at diagnosis, with relapsed disease, or with refractory disease may participate, provided that the diagnosis and disease status are established by the treating physician in accordance with national clinical practice and by the participating study center.

Enrolled patients will be reported and registered by means of a paper-based notification form sent by email to the Coordinating Center, which will assign a unique identification code to each patient.

At the time of notification, clinical and treatment-related data will be collected using a paper-based Case Report Form (CRF).

Biological material (peripheral blood, bone marrow, and/or tumor biopsy samples) must be centralized at the Laboratory of Experimental Oncology Therapies, IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini, Genoa, Italy, in accordance with the procedures described in the study protocol. Samples will be processed and analyzed as specified in the protocol.

The results of the initial analysis performed at CEINGE, Naples, will be communicated by the CEINGE Laboratory to the Coordinating Center. A multidisciplinary meeting will then be held with a panel of experts, including oncologists, biologists, pharmacists, and infectious disease specialists. Following this meeting, an individual report will be prepared for each patient.

The report will include the results of Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) or Cancer Gene Panel (CGP) analysis performed on the patient's DNA, together with any potential therapeutic recommendations based on the molecular alterations identified. The report will be sent to the physician responsible for the individual patient.

For patients who provide additional consent by signing the appropriate informed consent form, biological material may also be used for the following purposes:

i) Immunophenotyping, with particular focus on GD2 and B7-H3 expression in tumor biopsy samples and in neuroblastoma cells infiltrating the bone marrow;

ii) High-throughput screening of libraries comprising readily available anticancer drugs;

iii) Generation of in vitro and in vivo tumor models, including primary cell lines and spheroids in vitro, and murine models such as Patient-Derived Xenografts (PDX) and Cell Patient-Derived Xenografts (CPDX) at the Coordinating Center, as well as zebrafish models at San Martino-IST, Genoa, and/or Città della Speranza, Padua.
primary_outcomes: Molecular Profiling of Neuroblastoma to Identify Potential Therapeutic Targets
title: Prospective Multicenter Study of the Genomic, Transcriptomic, and Biological Profile of Patients With Neuroblastoma

brief_summary: Thin gingival phenotype may increase susceptibility to soft-tissue complications in the presence of local anatomical or mechanical risk factors. Minimally invasive injectable approaches such as injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF) and hyaluronic acid (HA) have been proposed to increase gingival thickness. This randomized split-mouth clinical trial compared repeated i-PRF and non-cross-linked HA injections in adults with a thin mandibular anterior gingival phenotype. Each participant received i-PRF on one mandibular anterior hemi-arch and HA on the contralateral hemi-arch. The primary objective was to compare changes in gingival thickness and keratinized tissue width between the two interventions. Periodontal clinical parameters and injection-related morbidity were assessed as secondary outcomes.
title: Injectable Platelet-Rich Fibrin Versus Hyaluronic Acid for Thin Gingival Phenotype

brief_summary: The creation of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) or direct intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (DIPS) results in an acute increase in venous return and cardiac preload. These procedures are established therapies for refractory ascites, variceal bleeding, hydrothorax, and Budd-Chiari syndrome, they may unmask subclinical cardiac dysfunction. Incidence of heart failure after TIPS varies widely from 0-25%, reflecting heterogeneity in patient selection and the lack of prospective data. Several predictors-including elevated pre-procedure BNP/NT-proBNP, diastolic dysfunction (E/e' \>10, LAVI \>34 mL/m²), impaired GLS, and elevated right-sided pressures-have been described, but most evidence arises from retrospective studies with inconsistent definitions.This single-center prospective cohort study at ILBS aims to determine the true incidence of heart failure within 6 months of TIPS/DIPS and to identify independent predictors using comprehensive clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic parameters. Heart failure is a clinical syndrome with symptoms and/or signs caused by structural and/or functional cardiac abnormality and corroborated by elevated natriuretic peptide levels and/or objective evidence of pulmonary or systemic congestion. In Echocardiography parameters GLS\<18 post TIPS for systolic function, E/e' average \> 15 for diastolic function will taken into consideration. In case of worsening diastolic function increase in grade of diastolic dysfunction ( measured by E/A)will be considered as post TIPS worsening.A total of 127 patients will be enrolled based on sample-size calculations assuming a 5% event rate. Findings will help create a clinically applicable predictive model to guide pre-TIPS cardiac risk stratification and optimize patient selection, thereby reducing morbidity and improving outcomes.
lead_sponsor: Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, India
primary_outcomes: Incidence of post TIPS/DIPS heart failure within first 6 months at ILBS
title: Incidence of Post TIPS/DIPS Heart Failure and the Factors Associated With Post-TIPS/DIPS Heart Failure.

brief_summary:
Post-labor analgesia intrapartum fever (PAIF) is a serious complication that increases the risk of cesarean delivery, postpartum bleeding, and health problems for newborns. Currently, doctors lack a simple tool to predict which mothers will develop a fever before they start labor analgesia.

This study aims to develop and test a computer prediction tool (using machine learning) to estimate the risk of PAIF. The investigators will review the medical records of mothers who received labor analgesia and delivered at term in three hospitals in China. Information that is available before the mothers receive analgesia, such as maternal age, gestational age, blood test results, and labor progress, will be collected. Using artificial intelligence, the investigators will build a prediction model. This model will then be tested on a separate group of women from a different hospital to ensure it works well in different settings. Finally, an open-access, interactive online calculator will be developed for clinicians.

The goal of this study is to provide doctors with a practical tool to quickly assess a mother's risk level before starting analgesia. This will help doctors monitor high-risk mothers more closely and prepare for possible complications. This study only uses existing medical records and will not change the routine care of any patients. Further studies will be needed to see if using this tool improves the health of mothers and babies.
lead_sponsor: Chengdu Jinjiang Maternity and Child Health Hospital
title: Machine Learning to Predict Fever After Labor Analgesia

This is a single-arm, multicenter clinical study evaluating the long-term effectiveness and safety profile of the CE-marked and commercially available Aveir leadless pacemaker systems manufactured by Abbott.

The study is largely based on a standard-of-care protocol, with the exception of an additional 24-hour Holter monitoring assessment in a selected group of patients after one year, as well as a CT scan (at UZ Leuven only) to accurately determine the position of the pacemaker. The aim of this study is to evaluate real-world safety, electrical performance, and clinical outcomes in patients for whom cardiac pacing is indicated and who will receive or have received one of the Aveir™ LP systems:

2. Aveir™ AR LP system, intended exclusively for atrial pacing

brief_summary: This multicenter randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of Shenfu Injection in preventing and treating ventilator dependence and ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction (VIDD) in critically ill adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive Shenfu Injection or control treatment in addition to standard clinical care. Diaphragm function will be monitored using daily bedside ultrasonography, including diaphragm excursion and diaphragm thickness. Clinical outcomes will include successful ventilator weaning, time to successful weaning, and the need for resumption of mechanical ventilation within 48 hours after initial weaning. The study is intended to determine whether Shenfu Injection can improve diaphragm function and facilitate liberation from mechanical ventilation.

brief_summary:
This is a Phase I, open-label, multicenter, dose-escalation study that aims to evaluate the safety and tolerability of intravesical inactivated Instillations of UPEC-FimON (Uro-Pathogenic E. coli) in participants with non-muscle invasive urothelial carcinoma (NMIUC) of the urinary bladder who failed previous Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) or intravesical chemotherapy.

Up to 30 participants will be enrolled, with 3 participants per cohort, following a dose-escalation model, with the potential for dose expansion. Dose-escalation and dose modification decisions will be based on an assessment of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), overall safety, and tolerability, and will be agreed upon by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB).
primary_outcomes: Safety and Tolerability of Inactivated UPEC-FimON administered intravesically
title: Phase I Study of Inactivated UPEC-FimON for Non Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer After BCG or Intravesical Chemotherapy Failure

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial evaluates the effects of a subacromial corticosteroid injection combined with a 12-week home-based exercise program in patients aged 18 to 60 years with supraspinatus tendinopathy. A total of 56 participants will be randomized into two groups. The intervention group will receive an ultrasound-guided subacromial-subdeltoid injection of 20 mg triamcinolone acetonide plus saline, while the placebo group will receive an ultrasound-guided intramuscular saline injection into the deltoid. Both groups will follow the same 12-week exercise program. The primary outcome is the change in supraspinatus tendon elasticity measured by shear wave elastography. Secondary outcomes include pain, shoulder function, disability, and quality of life assessed using VAS, Constant-Murley Score, QuickDASH, SPADI, and SF-12.
primary_outcomes: Change in Supraspinatus Tendon Elasticity Measured by Shear Wave Elastography
title: Subacromial Corticosteroid Injection Combined With Exercise in Supraspinatus Tendinopathy

brief_summary:
This is a descriptive observational study aimed at evaluating the inter-rater agreement of four behavioral rating scales used in pediatric dentistry-the Houpt Scale, the Ohio State University Behavioral Rating Scale, the Venham Scale, and the Frankl Scale-for assessing children's behavior during dental treatment. The study will be based on the analysis of video recordings of clinical procedures.

The study will include 30 children aged between 4 and 10 years who attend the Pediatric Dentistry postgraduate training clinic at the University of Valencia for dental treatment. Only children whose parents or legal guardians have signed the informed consent form for participation in the study, the consent form authorizing the dental treatment, and the consent form authorizing the use of images will be included.

Children classified as ASA III or IV, children with neurological or cognitive disorders, and children whose parents do not agree to participation or do not sign the informed consent form will be excluded. Clinical situations in which video recording could interfere with the safety of the procedure or compromise the patient's well-being will also be excluded.

The dental treatment will be performed by students enrolled in the postgraduate program in Pediatric Dentistry and will consist of restorative treatment for dental caries requiring local anesthesia.
primary_outcomes: Overall behavior during dental treatment assessed with the Houpt Behavior Rating Scale.
Child behavior during dental treatment assessed with the Ohio State University Behavioral Rating Scale (OSUBRS).
Dental anxiety during treatment assessed with the Venham Clinical Anxiety Rating Scale.
Child cooperation during dental treatment assessed with the Frankl Behavior Rating Scale.
title: Child Behavior Ratings During Dental Treatment

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical study was to learn whether a skincare regimen personalized by an artificial intelligence (AI) skin-analysis tool improves signs of facial skin aging in women aged 35 to 65 with mild-to-moderate facial photoaging. The main questions it aimed to answer were: Does the personalized regimen improve fine lines, wrinkles, firmness, smoothness, tone and other signs of skin aging after 4 and 12 weeks of use? Is the regimen well tolerated? Participants completed an online skin questionnaire and uploaded a facial selfie, and the AI tool assigned one of three night creams. Each participant then used a personalized kit at home for 12 weeks: a vitamin C serum and SPF 30 sunscreen in the morning; the assigned night cream (0.3% retinol, 0.6% retinol, or bakuchiol, each with a triple-peptide complex), an eye cream, and a dark spot remover in the evening; and a daily oral marine collagen supplement. Participants visited the clinic at baseline, week 4 and week 12 for expert skin grading, skin measurements, photographs and questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Expert-Graded Facial Photoaging Parameters (Modified Griffiths 10-Point Scale)
title: AI-Personalized Skincare Regimen for Facial Photoaging in Women

brief_summary:
This Phase 1 study is designed to evaluate the pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, bioavailability, safety, and tolerability effects of trigonelline monohydrate in generally healthy adults aged 40 to 70 years. Sixty participants will be randomized in a double-blind, parallel-arm study to receive one of four doses of trigonelline monohydrate (equivalent to 150 mg, 300 mg, 450 mg, or 600 mg of trigonelline daily), an active comparator (600 mg nicotinamide mononucleotide \[NMN\]), or placebo for 4 weeks.

The primary objective is to assess the effect of trigonelline monohydrate supplementation on NAD+ metabolism by measuring the change from baseline in whole blood NAD+ concentrations after 4 weeks of supplementation. Secondary objectives include evaluation of trigonelline pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, plasma accumulation following repeated dosing, effects on NAD-related metabolites, and urinary excretion of trigonelline and NAD-related metabolites. Safety and tolerability will be assessed through adverse events, vital signs, anthropometric measurements, and clinical laboratory assessments. Exploratory analyses will examine inflammatory biomarkers and additional NAD-related metabolic outcomes.
primary_outcomes: To assess the effect of TP daily supplementation on NAD metabolism, as measured by NAD+ concentrations in blood compared to placebo
title: Effects of Trigonelline Monohydrate on NAD+ Metabolism, Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability in Healthy Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether people living with severe psychiatric disorders can be grouped into more homogeneous subgroups, across usual diagnostic categories, based on two key dimensions: social withdrawal and anhedonia (reduced ability to feel pleasure). The study includes adolescents and adults aged 15 to 60 with schizophrenia, a first psychotic episode, bipolar disorder, recurrent or treatment-resistant major depressive disorder, or autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability, as well as healthy volunteers aged 18 to 60.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can subgroups of patients sharing a common profile of social withdrawal and anhedonia be identified, with similar clinical, genetic, biological and brain imaging characteristics?
* Do other dimensions (cognitive flexibility, neurodevelopmental, sensory and sleep disturbances, impulsivity) and specific clinical forms (e.g., autoimmune psychosis, metabolic abnormalities) define relevant subgroups, and how do these subgroups evolve over time? Researchers will compare patients with healthy volunteers to identify clinical and biological signatures specific to each subgroup.

Participants will:

* Attend an inclusion visit, two one-day assessment visits one year apart (clinical interviews, questionnaires, cognitive tests, fasting blood sample) and two brain MRI sessions
* Optionally provide a stool sample collected at home
* Complete questionnaires on a smartphone app and wear a connected watch (activity, sleep, heart rate) between visits
* Take part in the study for about 18 months French Minds is conducted in about 35 centres in France and aims to include 2,500 patients and 500 healthy volunteers.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants in each transdiagnostic subgroup defined by social withdrawal and anhedonia.
title: French Minds Cohort: a French Longitudinal and Multimodal Cohort of Patients With Major Mood Disorders, Psychotic Disorders, Autism Spectrum Disorders, and Healthy Controls

The study will be conducted in the postpartum service of a tertiary hospital. The results are expected to contribute to easily applicable, non-invasive, and supportive care approaches for breastfeeding support.

The study aims to describe their clinical, functional, neuropsychological, and psychosocial characteristics and to identify vulnerability factors potentially associated with disruption of follow-up during the transition to adult care. brief_summary:
The China Healthy Aging and Fitness Longitudinal Study (CHALF) is a nationwide prospective observational study designed to investigate how physical activity, exercise, and physical fitness are associated with health and aging among older adults in China.

The study plans to recruit approximately 8,960 adults aged 60-79 years from 14 provinces and provincial-level regions across China. Participants will complete questionnaires about their physical activity, exercise habits, lifestyle, nutrition, and health. They will also undergo standardized physical fitness assessments and blood tests.

Participants will be followed over time to track changes in physical fitness and health. Follow-up assessments will examine how physical activity, exercise, and physical fitness are associated with physical function, chronic diseases, and other health outcomes.

The findings will help improve understanding of healthy aging and provide evidence to support physical fitness monitoring and exercise guidance for older adults in China.
title: China Healthy Aging and Fitness Longitudinal Study

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the level of oral health knowledge and its relationship with caries experience, independently of age and sex, in adult patients attending a university dental clinic in Gran Canaria (Spain). Adults aged 19 years or older completed a validated 20-item oral health knowledge questionnaire and underwent a standardized clinical dental examination, complemented by a same-day panoramic radiograph obtained as part of routine care, to record the Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index according to World Health Organization criteria. The association between knowledge and the DMFT index was analyzed using negative binomial regression adjusted for age and sex.
lead_sponsor: University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
title: Oral Health Knowledge and Caries Experience in Adults

brief_summary:
After a stroke, some people have difficulty planning and carrying out familiar movements. This difficulty is called ideomotor apraxia and cannot be explained by muscle weakness alone. It may influence how people improve during rehabilitation.

This study will examine whether ideomotor apraxia is associated with changes in walking, balance, and independence in adults receiving rehabilitation after stroke at Izmir City Hospital.

Participants will be assessed for apraxia before rehabilitation and followed during their usual rehabilitation program, which includes conventional rehabilitation and RehaWalk-supported gait training. Walking and other functional abilities will be evaluated before and after the rehabilitation program. Changes will be compared between participants with and without apraxia.

The study will observe routine care. Participants will not be assigned to different treatments, and no experimental treatment will be provided. The findings may help clinicians understand whether apraxia is useful for predicting rehabilitation outcomes after stroke.
primary_outcomes: Change in Walking Speed on the 10-Meter Walk Test
title: Ideomotor Apraxia and Robotic Gait Rehabilitation Outcomes After Stroke

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to determine whether adding a serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) to a pectoralis II (PECS II) block improves pain relief and reduces the need for opioids in adult women undergoing breast removal surgery (mastectomy), with or without removal of lymph nodes from the armpit.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does adding an SAPB to a PECS II block reduce the total amount of opioids needed in the recovery room and during the first 24 hours after surgery?
2. Does the combination reduce the amount of opioid pain medication needed during surgery?
3. Does the combination improve pain levels during the first 24 hours after surgery?
4. Does the combination affect the occurrence of side effects or complications, including nausea, vomiting, drowsiness, serious reactions to the local anesthetic, and collapsed lung?

Researchers will compare a group receiving both SAPB and PECS II blocks with a group receiving only a PECS II block to determine whether the combination improves pain relief and reduces opioid requirements.

Participants will:

1. Be randomly assigned to one of two groups, with both groups receiving general anesthesia for surgery.
2. Receive the assigned nerve block or blocks using ultrasound guidance and a local anesthetic medicine called ropivacaine.
3. Receive postoperative pain relief through a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) device, which allows them to administer prescribed doses of morphine when needed, in addition to other pain medications.
4. Have their opioid use and pain levels assessed at scheduled intervals during the first 24 hours after surgery.
5. Be monitored for additional pain medication requirements, side effects, block-related complications, and changes in heart rate and blood pressure during surgery.
conditions: Mastectomy Plus Axillary Lymph Node Dissection
primary_outcomes: Cumulative perioperative opioid consumption till 24 hours postop
title: Effect of Serratus and Pectoralis II Plane Block Versus Pectoralis II Alone on Acute Postoperative Pain After Mastectomy

brief_summary:
Dental plaque is a major etiological factor in the development of gingivitis. Mechanical plaque control through toothbrushing is essential for maintaining oral hygiene, while toothpaste formulations containing active ingredients may provide additional benefits in controlling plaque accumulation and gingival inflammation. Enzymatic toothpaste containing the lactoperoxidase system and salt-containing toothpaste incorporating sodium chloride and sodium bicarbonate have been investigated for their potential effects on plaque control and gingival health.

This randomized, prospective, double-blind, parallel-group clinical study evaluated and compared the efficacy of enzymatic toothpaste, active salt toothpaste, and standard fluoridated toothpaste in reducing dental plaque and gingival inflammation following non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT).

The study was conducted in the Department of Periodontology, Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences, Saifai, Etawah, Uttar Pradesh, India, from July 2021 to December 2022. The study protocol received approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee of Uttar Pradesh University of Medical Sciences (approval number: 222/2020-21). Written informed consent was obtained from all participants before study procedures.

A total of 93 eligible participants with mild to moderate gingivitis were enrolled and randomly allocated to three groups. All participants initially received non-surgical periodontal therapy and used standard fluoridated toothpaste for a four-week pretreatment period. Following the pretreatment period, baseline clinical assessments were performed, and participants received the toothpaste assigned to the respective study group.

Group I received enzymatic toothpaste (Curaprox Enzycal 950), containing amyloglucosidase, glucose oxidase, lactoperoxidase, and potassium thiocyanate. Group II received active salt toothpaste (Colgate Active Salt), containing sodium chloride and sodium bicarbonate. Group III received standard fluoridated toothpaste (Colgate Strong Teeth), containing calcium carbonate and sodium monofluorophosphate.

Participants were instructed to brush their teeth for two minutes twice daily using the allocated toothpaste for 12 weeks. The use of mouthwashes, interdental aids, and other antiplaque products was restricted during the pretreatment and intervention periods.

Clinical assessments were performed at baseline, following the four-week pretreatment period, and after the 12-week intervention period, as specified in the study protocol. The clinical parameters included the Turesky-Gilmore-Glickman modification of the Quigley-Hein Plaque Index (TQHPI), the Gingival Index (GI), and probing pocket depth (PPD).

The collected data were analyzed using SPSS software, version 20.0. Within-group and between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric statistical tests. Statistical significance was set at p less than 0.05.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn which toric lens calculator best predicts the astigmatism remaining after cataract surgery in adults who received a TECNIS DIU toric intraocular lens (IOL) at Klinik Hietzing, Vienna, between January 2023 and March 2026.

Toric lenses correct astigmatism (an uneven curvature of the cornea) during cataract surgery. The strength of the lens and its orientation in the eye are chosen with online calculators. In an earlier study of the same patients, two widely used calculators - the Johnson \& Johnson toric calculator and the Barrett calculator of the European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgeons (ESCRS) - recommended different lenses in about 6 out of 10 eyes. It is not known which recommendation leads to the better result.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. In eyes in which the two calculators disagreed, which calculator predicted the astigmatism after surgery more accurately?
2. How accurate are four further calculator options, and did the toric lenses stay in their planned position?

Researchers will compare the astigmatism that each calculator predicted for the lens that was actually implanted with the astigmatism measured after surgery.

Participants will:

1. Attend one examination visit of about 60 to 90 minutes, at least 3 months after their cataract surgery
2. Have standard eye examinations: a vision test, a test for glasses (refraction), and several painless optical scans that do not touch the eye
3. Have the eye examined at the slit lamp; drops to widen the pupil are given only at the end of the visit, if needed, to check the position of the lens

No treatment, medication or surgery is given as part of this study.
primary_outcomes: Paired Difference in Alpins Difference Vector Magnitude Between the J&J Toric Calculator (PCA-ON) and ESCRS-Barrett in Eyes With Clinically Relevant Planning Discrepancy
title: Postoperative Outcome Verification of Discrepant Toric IOL Calculator Recommendations After Cataract Surgery

brief_summary:
Study Goal The goal of this multicenter, prospective observational cohort study is to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model that integrates portal hypertension, inflammation, and liver function indicators to predict the risk of adverse clinical outcomes (e.g., further decompensation, mortality, recompensation, and liver failure) in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.

Target Population The study will enroll adults aged 18-80 years with chronic liver disease of any etiology who have experienced at least one decompensating event (e.g., ascites, variceal bleeding, overt hepatic encephalopathy, jaundice, or infection requiring treatment) at or prior to enrollment.

Main Questions It Aims to Answer

1. How accurately can the multimodal model predict the risk of further decompensation (e.g., recurrent ascites, rebleeding, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, or hepatorenal syndrome-AKI) within 1 year of enrollment?
2. Can the model reliably predict 6-week, 1-year, and 2-year liver-related mortality, as well as the incidence of liver failure and the probability of recompensation (per Baveno VII criteria), and does it outperform traditional scoring systems?

Comparison Group Researchers will compare the performance of the newly developed multimodal model against established traditional prognostic tools, including the MELD, MELD-Na, and Child-Pugh scores, to assess whether the new model provides superior predictive accuracy, better risk reclassification, and greater clinical net benefit.

Participants Will

* Provide written informed consent before any study-related data collection.
* Undergo baseline and routine 3-month follow-up assessments (aligned with their standard clinical care) over a total of 3 years, during which clinical data, laboratory tests, and imaging results will be recorded.
* Voluntarily provide additional biospecimens (peripheral blood 10 mL, 3 stool tubes, and 10 mL urine) at baseline and during return visits for exploratory biomarker and multi-omics analysis (participants who provide samples receive a ¥200 nutritional subsidy; those undergoing clinically indicated MRI also receive free MRE testing).

brief_summary:
Colorectal cancer is a common cancer, that in general develops over a long time period (approximately 10-15 years) from precancerous polyps. The disease is in many cases asymptomatic. Colonoscopy allows doctors to examine the colon and rectum and identify colorectal cancer and/or precancerous growths, such as advanced adenomas. However, better methods are needed to identify patients that have precancerous lesions and early colorectal cancer and to understand the biological changes associated with these conditions.

The ProScreen study aims to investigate whether proteins measured in a blood sample can help distinguish between people with advanced precancerous growths, people with colorectal cancer, and people without these conditions.

In this first study, patients scheduled to undergo colonoscopy will be invited to participate and provide a blood sample. Participants will be classified according to the findings of their clinical examinations. Blood samples will be analyzed to measure multiple proteins and identify protein patterns associated with advanced precancerous growths and colorectal cancer.

The study does not involve an experimental treatment. The results may contribute to the development of improved blood tests for colorectal cancer prevention and early detection in the future.
primary_outcomes: Differences in blood protein profiles between controls, participants with advanced colorectal adenomas, and participants with colorectal cancer
title: Protein Signature Based Screening of Colorectal Adenomas and Cancer

People may be able to take part if they are adults with moderate to severe OSA, have overweight or obesity, and have been unable or unwilling using PAP therapy before joining the study. Participants will be assigned by chance to receive either berobenatide or a placebo (a treatment that looks like the study medicine but contains no active medicine). The study treatment will be given as an injection under the skin approximately once a month. Participants will receive study treatment at study sites and may administer some doses at home after receiving training.

During the study, participants will attend study visits, undergo sleep studies, complete questionnaires, and have health assessments performed. Researchers will compare the effects of berobenatide and placebo on sleep apnea, body weight, and other health measures.

brief_summary:
Chronic total occlusion (CTO) is defined as complete coronary occlusion with TIMI flow grade 0 persisting for more than three months, identified in 15-25% of patients undergoing coronary angiography.¹,² CTO is associated with refractory angina, left ventricular dysfunction, and increased long-term mortality.³ Revascularization aims to restore anterograde flow and improve myocardial perfusion; however, functional recovery-a patient-centered endpoint-remains variable and poorly predicted.⁴ ,⁵ Available data demonstrate that left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) alone is insufficient.⁵ ,⁶ Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived extracellular volume predicts recovery (OR 0.38; p=0.019), but CMR is not universally accessible.⁷ Stress echocardiography-derived myocardial work indices (GWI, GCW, GWE, GWW) have been validated in non-CTO populations, detecting dysfunction independent of LVEF and GLS, yet remain unstudied in CTO.⁸ ,⁹ Inflammatory biomarkers-monocyte-to-HDL ratio (MHR), soluble ST2 (sST2), and PIIINP-have shown prognostic value individually, but have not been integrated with myocardial work or procedural data.¹⁰ ,¹¹,¹² Procedural technique (antegrade vs. retrograde) affects procedural success but has not been evaluated as an independent predictor of functional recovery.¹³,¹⁴ The current strategy relies on fragmented, single-domain predictors, with no integrated pre-procedural model.

This research addresses that gap by combining mechanical (myocardial work), biological (MHR, sST2, PIIINP), and technical (procedural technique) domains into a unified predictive model. The rationale is that functional recovery is multifactorial, and an integrated model will outperform single-domain approaches, enabling better patient selection, procedural planning, and expectation setting.
conditions: Chronic Total Occlusions of Coronary Arteries
primary_outcomes: To develop an integrated predictive model combining stress echocardiography-derived myocardial work indices, inflammatory biomarkers (MHR, sST2, PIIINP), and procedural techniques to predict functional recovery after CTO revascularization.
title: Predicting Functional Recovery After Coronary Chronic Total Occlusion Revascularization

brief_summary:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common and disabling condition. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an established non-invasive neuromodulation treatment for depression, but clinical response varies considerably between individuals. One possible reason for this variability is that the effects of TMS may depend on the pattern of ongoing brain activity at the time stimulation is delivered.

This mechanistic, randomised, single-blind study will investigate whether synchronising TMS with transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), a form of weak electrical brain stimulation, can enhance the neurophysiological and cognitive effects of TMS in people experiencing a current moderate major depressive episode. The combined intervention is referred to as synchronised TMS (tsTMS).

Up to 60 participants will be recruited and randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: (1) TMS synchronised to the peak of a theta-frequency tACS waveform, (2) TMS synchronised to the trough of a theta-frequency tACS waveform, or (3) TMS combined with sham tACS. Participants will receive five daily neuromodulation sessions over one week.

The primary objective is to estimate variability in change in emotional processing, measured using the Cambridge Cognition Emotional Bias Task, in order to inform the design and sample size calculation of a future clinical trial. The study will also assess participant acceptability and tolerability of the intervention. Secondary objectives include exploring changes in brain oscillatory activity measured using electroencephalography (EEG), cognitive performance, mood and anxiety symptoms, functional outcomes, and digital biomarkers collected from an optional wearable device.

This study is designed to investigate mechanisms and feasibility rather than provide a full therapeutic course of TMS. Findings will be used to inform the development of a future definitive clinical trial evaluating whether synchronised neuromodulation can improve outcomes in depression.
primary_outcomes: Change in emotional bias (Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB) Emotional Bias task)
Frequency of adverse effects and tolerability
title: Dual Neuromodulation for Depression: Boosting TMS With tES

The study also compares the time needed to obtain results by each method and assesses participants' ease of use and satisfaction with the device. The aim is to determine whether this device could serve as a private, accessible screening tool for male fertility in Egypt.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of deoxycholate for the treatment of lipocytic ("fatty") deformities of the trunk and lower extremities; this includes areas such as cellulite or body contour deformities following liposuction. Ten participants will be enrolled in the pilot (part 1) portion of this study, and 60 participants will be enrolled in part 2 of this study (the blinded study).

Those who are eligible to be in the pilot (part 1) study will receive an injection with deoxycholate \[concentration of 10 mg/mL (1.0%)\] directly into the zone of fatty deformity.

Those who are eligible to be in the second part of this study will be randomly assigned to receive an injection with deoxycholate \[concentration of 10 mg/mL (1.0%)\] to one fatty deformity site, and an injection with a placebo (0.9% benzyl alcohol) without deoxycholate to a separate fatty deformity site. Thus, at each treatment session, participants will receive an injection with deoxycholate to one lipocytic deformity site, and an injection with a placebo to a separate (similar appearing) fatty deformity site. The placebo is provided for the comparator group.

Subsequent treatment visits will be conducted at approximately 28-day intervals for up to 5 treatment sessions (Visits 2, 3, 4, and 5 \[±5 days, relative to the date of the previous treatment session\]). Approximately 7 (±3) days after each treatment visit, participants will be required to come to the research site for Visits 1A, 2A, 3A, 4A, and 5A (relative to each treatment session) for evaluations of the treatment area, recording of vital signs and weight, and to update records on adverse events and concomitant medications. A post-treatment follow-up visit at 6 months (Visit 6 on Day 168) relative to the date of the initial treatment session will be required.

brief_summary:
Malnutrition and anemia are common among people with chronic kidney disease who receive maintenance hemodialysis. These conditions may worsen health outcomes and quality of life. Intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN) provides nutrients through a vein during hemodialysis and may be used when dietary intake is not sufficient. However, evidence on IDPN containing only amino acids, particularly in adults undergoing hemodialysis in Indonesia, remains limited.

This retrospective observational study will evaluate whether a 7.2% amino acid solution (KIDMIN®) given as IDPN is associated with improved nutritional status in adults with chronic kidney disease receiving maintenance hemodialysis. Medical records from Bangli Medika Canti Hospital covering July 2023 through December 2024 will be reviewed. Patients who received KIDMIN® during hemodialysis for at least 3 months will be compared with patients who did not receive IDPN. Both groups received the standard diet recommended for chronic kidney disease.

The main outcome is the change in serum albumin level from baseline to Month 3. Other outcomes include serum albumin through Month 6, hemoglobin levels, nutritional status assessed using the Subjective Global Assessment, and quality of life assessed using the Kidney Disease Quality of Life questionnaire. No study-specific medication or additional invasive procedure will be administered because the study uses previously available clinical data.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Albumin Level from Baseline to Month 3
title: Nutritional Status in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Receiving 7.2% Amino Acids During Hemodialysis

The protocol lists Severance Hospital, Gangnam Severance Hospital, and Yongin Severance Hospital as study sites. Planned enrollment is 1,550 participants: 1,500 adults aged 50 years or older and 50 healthy young adult controls aged 19-30 years.

Participants are enrolled according to eligibility criteria and consent, irrespective of the specific medication received. Clinical information, cognitive assessments, and available brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) data will be collected to investigate diagnosis, disease severity, and clinical course. A total of 6 mL of research blood will be collected for banking, separated into plasma and buffy coat, and stored at -70°C. Young adult controls will provide a comparison for age-related and disease-related biomarker differences. The target follow-up duration for the memory disorder cohort is 5 years; young adult controls attend a single study visit. The overall study period is 120 months from IRB approval.

brief_summary: This study was conducted to assess the impact of AI-supported climate change education on adolescents' awareness of global climate change and their levels of concern about climate change. The study was conducted at a middle school affiliated with the Ministry of National Education in a province in the Southeastern Anatolia Region between December 2025 and September 2026, using a pre-test-post-test control group experimental design. The population of the study consists of 8th-grade students attending middle schools in the province. The schools from which data were collected were selected using a random draw. The study was conducted with a total of 120 students, comprising an experimental group (n=60) and a control group (n=60). Students in the experimental group received artificial intelligence-supported climate change education using virtual reality (VR) headsets. Data were collected using the Data Collection Form, the Climate Change Worry Scale (CCWS), and the Global Climate Change Awareness Scale (GCCAS). Descriptive statistics, chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, t-tests for dependent and independent samples, and ANOVA for mixed-design repeated measures were used in the analysis of the data. Effect sizes were assessed using partial eta-squared (η²p) and Cohen's d. Ethical principles were adhered to throughout the study. According to the research findings, the baseline characteristics of the experimental and control groups were found to be similar (p \> 0.05). It was found that the average GCCAS and CCwS scores of the experimental group increased following AI-supported education (p\<0.001). In the control group, however, it was determined that the pre-test to post-test changes in GCCAS and CCWS scores were not statistically significant (p \> 0.05). It was found that time × group interactions were significant for GCCAS and CCWS, and that there were differences of large effect size in favor of the experimental group on the final test. It was found that AI-supported climate change education increases adolescents' awareness of global climate change and also leads to an increase in their levels of concern about climate change. In this regard, it is recommended that AI-supported educational programs be used in school health practices to enhance adolescents' awareness of climate change; and that school health nurses monitor students' emotional responses to climate change to help balance rising anxiety through appropriate coping strategies, self-efficacy, and support mechanisms.
interventions: AI-Supported Climate Change Education Using Virtual Reality
primary_outcomes: the Global Climate Change Awareness Scale
title: The Effect of AI-Supported Climate Change Education on Adolescents' Levels of Awareness and Concern

brief_summary:
Dysautonomia of Adolescence (dysautonomia) is an umbrella term used to describe symptoms experienced by adolescents and young adults related to dysfunction of the autonomic nervous system. Symptoms can include dizziness, fatigue, increased heart rate upon standing, exercise intolerance, and difficulty with daily activities. Treatment commonly involves lifestyle modifications, including increased fluid and salt intake and structured routines related to diet, sleep, aerobic exercise, and lower-body strength training. While these approaches can be effective, some patients experience symptoms that make it difficult to implement these changes.

Despite increasing awareness of dysautonomia, research evaluating effective treatment strategies in adolescents remains limited, and there are currently no medications approved by Health Canada specifically for the treatment of dysautonomia. Ivabradine is a heart rate-lowering medication approved for the treatment of heart failure and has been studied as a potential treatment for symptoms associated with dysautonomia, including postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS). However, there is limited evidence regarding its use in adolescents.

The purpose of this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study is to evaluate whether ivabradine can reduce symptom burden and improve heart rate control and overall well-being in adolescents with dysautonomia. The study will use a series of N-of-1 randomized controlled trials in which participants receive both ivabradine and placebo during different treatment periods. This design will allow the effects of ivabradine and placebo to be compared within individual participants.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Resting Heart Rate (bpm) at end of 4-week treatment period.
title: Effect of Ivabradine on Adolescent Dysautonomia
